exEn: We have to check in two hours before.
note: ch is pronounced like tj. Airport signs say Incheckning (check-in).

exEn: Where do you pick up the luggage?
note: French loan: the last g is the sj-sound. Handbagage = carry-on.

exEn: My suitcase never arrived.

ex: Vi kom igenom {säkerhetskontrollen} på fem minuter.
exEn: We got through security in five minutes.
Excuse me, where's the exit?
note: At the airport, utgång also means gate: utgång 12.

exEn: See you at the entrance at seven.
We're flying to Thailand in February.
note: Irregular: flög, flugit.

exEn: The plane took off an hour late.
note: Also the everyday word for lifting something: lyfta en låda.

ex: Planet {landar} på Arlanda kvart över tre.
exEn: The plane lands at Arlanda at a quarter past three.
How was the trip?
note: Also a verb: resa (to travel).

exEn: She travels a lot for work.
note: For everyday trips, åka is more common: åka till jobbet.

exEn: Bye, and have a nice trip!
We're on vacation all of July.
note: Time off from work: vara på semester = to be on vacation. Plural semestrar.

ex: Gamla stan är full av {turister} på sommaren.
exEn: The Old Town is full of tourists in the summer.
Are you going abroad this summer?
note: Used for both place and direction: bo utomlands, resa utomlands.

exEn: Can you show me on the map?
Can you send directions?
note: Singular in Swedish where English says directions.

exEn: Have you booked the hotel?
I haven't packed yet.
We got on the bus at the square.
note: Irregular: steg, stigit. In speech often gå på. Stig på! also means Come in!

ex: Jag ska {stiga av} vid nästa hållplats.
exEn: I'm getting off at the next stop.
note: In speech, gå av is very common: Jag går av här.

exEn: You have to change trains in Hallsberg.
note: Also to exchange: byta en tröja i affären.

exEn: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus!
note: To miss a person is sakna: Jag saknar dig.

exEn: Call when you've arrived!
note: Irregular like komma: kom fram, kommit fram.

exEn: Are we almost there?
note: Nu är vi framme! = We're here!

ex: Jag tog {körkort} när jag var arton.
exEn: I got my driver's license when I was eighteen.
note: Ta körkort = to get your license. Also a common form of ID in Sweden.

exEn: There's a lot of traffic in the morning.

ex: Vi stod i {kö} på motorvägen i en timme.
exEn: We were stuck in traffic on the highway for an hour.
note: Stå i kö = to wait in line, in a shop or in traffic.

ex: Det har hänt en {olycka} på E4:an.
exEn: There's been an accident on the E4.
note: Also misfortune. A traffic accident is a trafikolycka.

exEn: He was driving at high speed.
We're running out of gas.
note: Stressed on the last syllable: ben-SIN.

ex: Vi måste {tanka} innan vi kör vidare.
exEn: We need to fill up before we drive on.
note: A gas station is a bensinstation, or a mack in everyday speech.

exEn: Where can you park around here?
I'm going to buy groceries after work.
note: The everyday word for buying food: handla mat. Handla om = to be about: Filmen handlar om en hund.

ex: Vi var på stan och {shoppade} hela dagen.
exEn: We were in town shopping all day.
note: sh is the sj-sound. Used for clothes and fun things; buying food is handla.

exEn: We're going to sell our old car.
note: Irregular: sålde, sålt.

exEn: I don't have any money left.
note: Always plural in Swedish: Pengarna räcker inte (The money isn't enough).

exEn: The ice cream costs twenty-five kronor.
note: Plural kronor, written kr or SEK: 25 kr. Krona also means crown.

ex: Priset är nitton kronor och nittio {öre}.
exEn: The price is nineteen kronor and ninety öre.
note: There are no öre coins any more, but prices still use them: 19,90 kr. Cash totals are rounded to whole kronor.

exEn: The machine only takes coins.
note: Same form in the plural: ett mynt, två mynt.

exEn: Can you break this bill?
note: The e drops in the plural: sedlar. In everyday speech: en hundralapp (a 100-kronor note).

exEn: Many stores don't take cash anymore.
note: Plural only. To pay cash = betala kontant.

exEn: Here you go, keep the change!
note: No plural in this sense. Also means gear (in a car).

exEn: I've left my card at home.
note: Same spelling as kort (short). Any card: vykort (postcard), körkort (driver's license).

ex: Hon fick ett {presentkort} på femhundra kronor.
exEn: She got a gift card worth five hundred kronor.

alt: can I pay with a card
can I pay with my card
ex: Jag har inga kontanter. {Kan jag betala med kort}?
exEn: I don't have any cash. Can I pay by card?
note: Cards are accepted almost everywhere in Sweden. Also: Tar ni kort?

exEn: You can send me the money by Swish.
note: Swish is the mobile payment app almost everyone in Sweden uses. Pronounced svisha.

exEn: Prices have gone up this year.
note: Also means prize: Hon vann första pris.

ex: Ursäkta, {hur mycket kostar det} att parkera här?
exEn: Excuse me, how much does it cost to park here?
note: Also: Vad kostar det? About a specific thing: Hur mycket kostar den?

exEn: That'll be a hundred and fifty kronor, please.
note: What the cashier says when telling you the total.

exEn: Students get a ten percent discount.
note: Stress on -batt. Also means a flower bed.

exEn: I bought the shoes on sale.
note: På rea = on sale. Det är rea! = There's a sale on! Short for realisation.

ex: Butiken har ett bra {erbjudande} på kaffe.
exEn: The store has a good deal on coffee.
note: From erbjuda (to offer). Stores advertise Veckans erbjudande (This week's offer).

exEn: You pay at the checkout over there.
note: Many supermarkets also have självscanning (self-scanning).

exEn: Would you like the receipt?
note: Keep it! You usually need it to return or exchange something.

ex: – {Var det bra så}? – Ja, det var allt.
exEn: – Will that be all? – Yes, that's everything.
note: Very common at shop and café counters. Literally: Was that good like that?

exEn: Do you need a bag?
note: Bags cost a few kronor at the checkout, so many people bring their own. A handbag is a väska.

ex: Ska vi ta en {kundvagn} eller en korg?
exEn: Shall we take a cart or a basket?
note: kund (customer) + vagn (cart); gn sounds like ngn. Some stores need a coin to unlock the carts.

exEn: I'm putting the fruit in the basket.
note: rg at the end sounds like rj. Online, your cart is varukorgen.

en: to stand in line; to queue
exEn: We had to stand in line for half an hour.
note: Hard k, as in kö (unlike köpa, which starts with the tj-sound).

ex: Vad har ni för {öppettider} i jul?
exEn: What are your opening hours over Christmas?
note: Almost always plural; the singular öppettid is rare.

ex: Affären {har öppet} till nio i kväll.
exEn: The store is open until nine tonight.
note: The opposite is ha stängt. Signs on doors just say Öppet / Stängt.

exEn: The store sells goods from all over the world.
note: Mostly plural: varor = goods. Not the same word as the verb vara (to be).

exEn: What size are you?
note: Sizes are European: Jag har storlek 40 i skor (I take a size 40 shoe).

sv: Finns den i en större storlek?
en: do you have it in a bigger size?
alt: do you have it in a bigger size
do you have it in a larger size
does it come in a bigger size
do you have a bigger size
ipa: fɪnːs dɛn ɪ ɛn ˈstœrːɛ ˈstuːˌɭeːk
ex: Tröjan är för liten. {Finns den i en större storlek}?
exEn: The sweater is too small. Do you have it in a bigger size?
note: Smaller: i en mindre storlek. Literally: Does it exist in a bigger size?

exEn: Can I try on these pants?
note: Also to try in general: Prova den här kakan! (Try this cake!)

exEn: Excuse me, where are the fitting rooms?
note: prova (to try on) + hytt (cabin).

ex: – Kan jag hjälpa dig? – Nej tack, {jag tittar bara}.
exEn: – Can I help you? – No thanks, I'm just looking.
note: The polite answer when a shop assistant offers help.

ex: Jag vill {lämna tillbaka} de här skorna.
exEn: I'd like to return these shoes.
note: Stress on tillbaka. Få pengarna tillbaka = to get a refund.

ex: Telefonen gick sönder, så jag {reklamerade} den.
exEn: The phone broke, so I took it back as faulty.
note: False friend: not reclaim. You can complain to the seller about faulty goods for up to three years.

exEn: The phone has a two-year warranty.
note: Stress on -ti. Definite form: garantin.

ex: Jag köpte en {begagnad} cykel på nätet.
exEn: I bought a used bike online.
note: gn sounds like ngn: be-GANG-nad.

ex: I helgen ska vi gå på {loppis}.
exEn: This weekend we're going to a flea market.
note: Short for loppmarknad. Gå på loppis = go to a flea market or second-hand sale.

ex: Jag måste köpa en {present} till Anna.
exEn: I have to buy a present for Anna.
note: Stress on -sent. A Christmas present is a julklapp.

exEn: I'm saving money for a trip.
note: Also to save a file, and to keep: Spara kvittot! (Keep the receipt!)

ex: Hon {tjänar} bra på sitt nya jobb.
exEn: She makes good money at her new job.
note: Starts with the tj-sound. Also means to serve.

ex: Vi {har råd} med en större lägenhet nu.
exEn: We can afford a bigger apartment now.
note: ha råd med + noun, ha råd att + verb. Jag har inte råd = I can't afford it.

ex: Kan jag {låna} hundra kronor av dig?
exEn: Can I borrow a hundred kronor from you?
note: låna av = borrow from. To lend is låna ut: Kan du låna ut din cykel?

ex: Vi tog ett {lån} för att köpa huset.
exEn: We took out a loan to buy the house.
note: ta ett lån = take out a loan. A mortgage is ett bolån.

exEn: I need to open a bank account.
note: Often just kontot: Pengarna finns på kontot.

exEn: He's looking for work in healthcare.
note: A bit formal; in everyday speech people say jobb: på jobbet = at work.

exEn: I've got a new job!
note: Same form in the plural: ett jobb, två jobb.

exEn: She wants to change careers.
He works for a big company.
note: Same form in the plural: ett företag, två företag.

exEn: My workplace is near the station.
We get paid on the 25th of every month.
note: Payday (lönedag) in Sweden is usually the 25th.

exEn: I have to ask my boss first.
note: False friend: a chef (cook) is en kock. Ch is said like sj.

exEn: I have lunch with my colleagues.
note: The plural kolleger is also correct. Stress on -le-.

exEn: She's employed at a bank.
note: Also used as a noun: en anställd (an employee), de anställda (the employees).

exEn: My employer is paying for the course.
note: Literally 'work giver'. The g in -givare is soft, like j.

ex: Det var många {kunder} i butiken idag.
exEn: There were a lot of customers in the shop today.

ex: Jag sitter i {möte}, kan jag ringa dig sen?
exEn: I'm in a meeting, can I call you later?
note: Sitta i möte = to be in a meeting. The verb is möta (to meet).

exEn: I work full-time at a warehouse.
note: Jobba heltid = to work full-time; a full-time job is ett heltidsjobb.

exEn: She works part-time while she's studying.
note: Jobba deltid = to work part-time; a part-time job is ett deltidsjobb.

exEn: We had to work overtime all week.

ex: Han har varit {arbetslös} i ett halvår.
exEn: He has been unemployed for six months.
note: Arbetsförmedlingen, the public employment service, helps people find work.

exEn: She's on sick leave for the rest of the week.
note: After seven days off sick you need a doctor's note (läkarintyg).

exEn: My husband is on parental leave this spring.
note: Swedish parents share 480 days of paid parental leave per child.

ex: Du kan {ansöka} om jobbet via vår hemsida.
exEn: You can apply for the job on our website.
note: Ansöka om + noun. In everyday speech people just say söka: söka jobb.

exEn: I sent my application yesterday.
note: Irregular: the definite form is also ansökan, and the plural is ansökningar.

exEn: I'm nervous about the interview tomorrow.
note: Stress on the last syllable: inter-VJU.

ex: Skicka ditt {CV} och ett personligt brev.
exEn: Send your résumé and a cover letter.
note: Said like the letters: 'say-vay'. A cover letter is ett personligt brev.

ex: Har du {erfarenhet} av att jobba med barn?
exEn: Do you have experience working with children?
note: Erfarenhet av = experience of or with. An experience you live through is en upplevelse.

exEn: The company is going to hire ten new people.

ex: Hon har fått en fast {anställning} på skolan.
exEn: She has got a permanent job at the school.
note: Fast anställning = permanent job; tidsbegränsad anställning = temporary job.

exEn: The factory laid off a hundred people.
note: Also to cancel a contract: säga upp lägenheten. Being fired is få sparken (informal).

ex: Han {sa upp sig} och startade ett eget företag.
exEn: He quit his job and started his own company.
note: The pronoun changes: jag sa upp mig, hon sa upp sig. In everyday speech you can also say sluta.

ex: Jag gör {praktik} på ett hotell i tre månader.
exEn: I'm doing an internship at a hotel for three months.
note: Göra praktik = to do an internship or work placement, often as part of a course.

ex: Min pappa går i {pension} nästa år.
exEn: My dad is retiring next year.
note: Gå i pension = to retire; a retiree is en pensionär. Said 'pang-SHOON'.

exEn: I'm taking Friday off.
note: The g in ledigt is silent. Vara ledig = to be off work.

ex: Min första {uppgift} var att svara i telefon.
exEn: My first task was to answer the phone.
note: Also means information or details: personuppgifter = personal details.

exEn: The hotel staff were really friendly.
note: False friend: personal means staff. 'Personal' is personlig.

alt: What do you do for a living?
What do you do for work?
ex: Trevligt att träffas! {Vad jobbar du med}?
exEn: Nice to meet you! What do you do?
note: Answer without an article: Jag är sjuksköterska (I'm a nurse).

exEn: I work as a carpenter in Uppsala.
note: No article before the job: Jag jobbar som lärare = I work as a teacher.

exEn: She works as a doctor in the ER.
note: The official word; doktor is common in speech. Same form in the plural: två läkare.

exEn: The nurse is taking a blood sample.
note: Two sj-sounds: sjuk- and -skö-. Used for both women and men.

ex: Han jobbar som {undersköterska} på ett äldreboende.
exEn: He works as an assistant nurse at a care home.
note: One of the most common jobs in Swedish healthcare and elderly care.

ex: Jag har en tid hos {tandläkaren} på tisdag.
exEn: I have a dentist appointment on Tuesday.
note: Literally 'tooth doctor'.

exEn: Our teacher speaks slowly and clearly.
note: Same form in the plural: en lärare, två lärare. Definite plural: lärarna.

exEn: My wife is a preschool teacher.
note: förskola (preschool) + lärare (teacher).

exEn: My brother is a police officer in Gothenburg.
note: En polis = a police officer; polisen = the police. Emergency number: 112.

exEn: The firefighters came after five minutes.
note: Irregular plural like man: brandmän, brandmännen. Used for women too.

ex: Han är {kock} på en italiensk restaurang.
exEn: He's a chef at an Italian restaurant.
note: English 'chef' is kock; en chef is a boss!

exEn: She's an engineer and builds bridges.
note: The g is an sj-sound: in-sje-NJÖR.

exEn: There are lots of jobs for programmers.
note: Stress on -me-. Also common: utvecklare (developer).

ex: {Snickaren} bygger ett nytt kök åt oss.
exEn: The carpenter is building a new kitchen for us.
We have to call an electrician.
note: Same form in the plural: en elektriker, två elektriker.

exEn: I'm going to the hairdresser's on Saturday.
note: Klippa sig = to get a haircut.

exEn: My grandfather was a farmer in Småland.
note: Irregular plural with ö: bönder, bönderna.

exEn: You should talk to a lawyer.
note: Stress on the last syllable: advo-KAT.

ex: Hon jobbar som {säljare} i en klädbutik.
exEn: She works as a sales assistant in a clothing store.
note: From sälja (to sell).

exEn: The cleaners come every evening after six.
note: From städa (to clean). Job words in -are have the same form in the plural.

exEn: The bus driver said good morning to everyone.
note: Chaufför (driver) comes from French; ch is said like sj.

ex: Hon jobbar som {journalist} på en tidning.
exEn: She works as a journalist at a newspaper.
note: The j is an sj-sound, as in French.

exEn: She's a researcher at Lund University.
note: From forska (to do research). Rs is pronounced like sh.

ex: Hennes pappa är {konstnär} och målar tavlor.
exEn: Her dad is an artist and paints pictures.
note: A painter or sculptor; a performer (singer, musician) is en artist.

exEn: The kids bike to school every morning.
note: gå i skolan = to go to (attend) school; i skolan = at school.

ex: Jag hämtar barnen på {förskolan} klockan fyra.
exEn: I pick up the kids from preschool at four.
note: For children aged 1–5. Many people still call it dagis.

ex: Efter {grundskolan} börjar de flesta på gymnasiet.
exEn: After compulsory school, most people start upper secondary school.
note: Years 1–9 (about ages 7–16), free and compulsory for all children.

ex: Min bror går sista året på {gymnasiet}.
exEn: My brother is in his last year of high school.
note: False friend: not a gym (that's ett gym). Usually definite: gå på gymnasiet.

ex: Min syster pluggar på {universitetet} i Göteborg.
exEn: My sister studies at the university in Gothenburg.
note: Stressed on the last syllable: u-ni-ver-si-TET. Same form in the plural.

ex: Jag vill söka till {högskolan} nästa år.
exEn: I want to apply to college next year.
note: Not a high school! It's higher education, like a universitet but usually smaller.

ex: Jag går på {sfi} tre dagar i veckan.
exEn: I go to SFI three days a week.
note: Svenska för invandrare: free Swedish classes for adults new to Sweden. Said as letters (ess-eff-i), used without an article. Also written SFI.

exEn: There are twenty-five students in our class.
note: School years are named by number: Hon går i trean = she's in third grade.

ex: Det är alldeles för varmt i {klassrummet}.
exEn: It's way too warm in the classroom.
note: The m doubles before an ending: klassrummet, klassrummen.

exEn: The school has about five hundred pupils.
note: A pupil at school (also at sfi); at a university you are a student.

exEn: Many students work part-time on weekends.
note: ta studenten = to graduate from upper secondary school, a big celebration with white caps.

exEn: The principal wants to talk to your parents.
note: Also the head of a university. The stress moves in the plural: rektorer is stressed on -tor-.

exEn: The lesson starts at a quarter past eight.
note: -tion is pronounced 'shoon' with the sj-sound.

exEn: Which subject do you like best?
note: Also a topic: byta ämne = to change the subject.

exEn: Have you done your math homework?
note: Countable in Swedish: en läxa (one assignment), många läxor.

exEn: We have an English test tomorrow.
note: skriva prov = to take a test. Same form in the plural.

exEn: She got the highest grade in Swedish.
note: School grades go from A (best) to E (lowest pass); F is a fail.

ex: Jag går en {kurs} i spanska på kvällarna.
exEn: I'm taking a Spanish course in the evenings.
note: gå en kurs = to take a course. The u is short.

exEn: The program takes three years.
note: Education in general, or one study program: en treårig utbildning (a three-year program).

exEn: He graduated in June.
note: Not an exam: ta examen = to graduate. Irregular: the definite form is also examen, the plural examina.

ex: På {rasten} spelar vi fotboll på skolgården.
exEn: At recess we play soccer in the schoolyard.
note: Also a break at work: lunchrast = lunch break.

ex: Har du sett {schemat} för nästa vecka?
exEn: Have you seen the schedule for next week?
note: sch is the sj-sound, as in schampo.

exEn: The new semester starts in August.
note: False friend: semester means vacation in Swedish! hösttermin = fall semester, vårtermin = spring semester.

exEn: The kids are off school all next week.
note: School breaks: sommarlov, jullov, sportlov. Working adults have semester instead.

ex: Jag har lånat en {bok} på biblioteket.
exEn: I've borrowed a book from the library.
note: Irregular plural: en bok, två böcker.

exEn: Open your books to page twenty.
note: Also a side: på andra sidan gatan = across the street.

exEn: Can I borrow a pen?
note: Any pen or pencil. To be exact: blyertspenna (pencil), kulspetspenna (ballpoint pen).

exEn: Write your name at the top of the paper.
note: Also documents: Har du dina papper? (Do you have your papers?)

exEn: Cut out the picture with a pair of scissors.
note: Singular in Swedish: en sax = a pair of scissors.

exEn: The teacher writes the words on the board.
note: Also a painting or picture on the wall.

exEn: Look the word up in a dictionary.
note: slå upp = to look up. Plural like bok: ordböcker.

exEn: How long have you been studying Swedish?
note: Languages are lowercase in Swedish. en svenska also means a Swedish woman.

exEn: We have English every Tuesday.
note: Many language names end in -ska: engelska, svenska, tyska, franska, spanska.

exEn: Math is my favorite subject.
note: Short for matematik.

exEn: He's very interested in history.
note: Also a story: Berätta en historia! (Tell me a story!)

exEn: How many languages do you speak?
note: Same form in the plural: ett språk, två språk.

exEn: What does this word mean?
note: Same form in the plural: ett ord, två ord.

exEn: Write a sentence with each word.
note: Also meaning or purpose: Vad är meningen med det? (What's the point of that?)

exEn: Your pronunciation is getting better and better!
note: From uttala (to pronounce): Hur uttalar man det här?

exEn: May I ask a question?
note: ställa en fråga = to ask a question. Also a verb: fråga (to ask).

exEn: Do you know the answer to question three?
note: svaret på = the answer to. The verb is svara (to answer).

exEn: Do exercise five for next time.
note: Övning ger färdighet = practice makes perfect.

ex: Alla gör {misstag} när de lär sig ett språk.
exEn: Everyone makes mistakes when they learn a language.
note: göra ett misstag = to make a mistake. In speech, people also say göra fel.

ex: Alla i klassen blev {godkända} på provet.
exEn: Everyone in the class passed the test.
note: bli godkänd = to pass; the opposite is underkänd (failed). Many courses grade G (pass), VG (pass with distinction) or U (fail).

ex: Jag måste {plugga} inför provet på fredag.
exEn: I have to study for the test on Friday.
note: The everyday word for studying; studera sounds more formal.

exEn: She's studying law in Uppsala.
note: In speech Swedes often say läsa: Jag läser svenska = I'm studying Swedish.

ex: Barn {lär sig} nya språk väldigt snabbt.
exEn: Children learn new languages very quickly.
note: sig changes with the person: jag lär mig, du lär dig, vi lär oss.

exEn: Dad taught me to ride a bike.
note: lära någon något = to teach someone something. With sig it means to learn.

exEn: I practice my pronunciation every day.
note: öva på något = to practice something.

exEn: How do you spell your last name?
note: Hur stavas det? = How is that spelled?

ex: Jag är {sjuk} och stannar hemma idag.
exEn: I'm sick and staying home today.
note: Bli sjuk = to get sick. Sj is the breathy sj-sound.

exEn: Now I'm well again!
note: Not 'frisky'. Bli frisk = to get well. It also means 'fresh': frisk luft (fresh air).

exEn: Smoking is bad for your health.
note: Don't mix it up with the verb hälsa (to greet).

exEn: Diabetes is a common disease.
I'm not feeling very well today.
note: Hur mår du? = How are you? Må bra / må dåligt = to feel good / to feel bad.

ex: Jag {mår illa} och vill inte äta.
exEn: I feel nauseous and don't want to eat.
note: It means nausea, not just feeling bad: for that, say må dåligt.

exEn: I'm so tired today.
note: Trött på = tired of: Jag är trött på regnet.

ex: Jag blir {yr} när jag reser mig.
exEn: I get dizzy when I stand up.
My head hurts.
note: Ha ont i + body part in the definite form: ont i magen, ont i halsen.

exEn: It hurts when I walk.
note: Aj, det gör ont! = Ouch, that hurts!

exEn: My back is aching.
note: A dull, lasting pain. Common in compounds: huvudvärk, tandvärk.

exEn: How bad is the pain right now?
note: More formal than ont; used by doctors and on medicine packages.

ex: Jag har {huvudvärk} och vill vila lite.
exEn: I have a headache and want to rest a bit.
note: No article: Jag har huvudvärk. Also: Jag har ont i huvudet.

exEn: The kids got a stomachache from all the ice cream.
note: Also: ont i magen.

ex: Drick te med honung om du har {halsont}.
exEn: Drink tea with honey if you have a sore throat.
note: Also: ont i halsen.

ex: Jag har {tandvärk} och måste till tandläkaren.
exEn: I have a toothache and have to go to the dentist.

ex: Han har haft hög {feber} sedan igår.
exEn: He has had a high fever since yesterday.
note: No article: Jag har feber (I have a fever).

exEn: I have a bit of a cold today.
note: Swedes usually say Jag är förkyld rather than Jag har en förkylning.

exEn: It's just a common cold.
note: k before y is soft (the tj-sound): för-TJYL-ning.

ex: Många är sjuka i {influensa} just nu.
exEn: Lots of people have the flu right now.
note: Sjuk i influensa = sick with the flu. Colloquially also flunsa.

ex: Jag har haft {hosta} i två veckor.
exEn: I've had a cough for two weeks.
note: No article: Jag har hosta (I have a cough).

exEn: He coughed all night.

ex: Jag har {snuva} och ont i halsen.
exEn: I have a runny nose and a sore throat.
note: A stuffy nose is täppt näsa: Jag är täppt i näsan.

exEn: I'm sneezing all the time.
note: Past also nyste. When someone sneezes, say Prosit! (Bless you!)

exEn: She's been throwing up all night.
note: An -s verb in every form: kräks, kräktes, kräkts. In everyday speech also spy.

exEn: Do you have any allergies?
note: Stress on the last syllable, and the g is hard. Allergisk mot = allergic to.

ex: Är det {smittsamt}? Kan jag gå till jobbet?
exEn: Is it contagious? Can I go to work?
note: From smitta: infection (noun) or to infect (verb).

exEn: My arm itches.
note: Usually with det: Det kliar (It itches).

exEn: It's not a serious injury.
note: Also a verb: skada (to injure, to damage).

exEn: She fell and hurt herself.
note: Reflexive: jag skadar mig, du skadar dig, hon skadar sig.

exEn: Wash the wound with soap and water.
Your nose is bleeding!

ex: Jag fick ett stort {blåmärke} på benet.
exEn: I got a big bruise on my leg.
note: Literally 'blue mark'.

exEn: He has broken his arm.
note: Irregular: bröt, brutit. Use the definite form for your own body: bryta benet. Broken = bruten (benet är brutet).

exEn: She fainted in the heat.
The ambulance came after ten minutes.
note: The ending is usually said -angs, as in many French loanwords.

exEn: Quick, call an ambulance!
note: The emergency number in Sweden is 112 (ett ett två).

ex: Vi åkte till {akuten} mitt i natten.
exEn: We went to the ER in the middle of the night.
note: Almost always used in the definite form: akuten. As an adjective, akut means 'acute, urgent'.

exEn: You should go to the doctor.
note: The official word is läkare; doktor is common in speech and as a title.

en: I need to see a doctor
exEn: I need to see a doctor today.
note: Träffa (to meet) is also used for seeing a doctor.

exEn: The patient can go home today.
note: The ti is said like 'si': pa-si-ENT.

ex: Jag har en {tid} hos läkaren klockan tre.
exEn: I have a doctor's appointment at three.
note: Usually 'time'; in healthcare, en tid is an appointment.

exEn: I called the health center and made an appointment.
note: You can often book online through 1177.se.

en: to call the health advice line
ex: Om du blir sämre kan du {ringa 1177}.
exEn: If you get worse, you can call 1177.
note: 1177 (elva sjuttiosju) is Sweden's healthcare advice line, open 24/7. In an emergency, call 112.

exEn: The doctor examined my knee.
note: En undersökning = an examination, a check-up.

ex: – {Var gör det ont}? – Här, i knät.
exEn: – Where does it hurt? – Here, in my knee.
Breathe calmly and deeply.
note: An -s verb in every form: andas, andades, andats. Andas in / ut = breathe in / out.

ex: Läkaren skrev ut ett {recept} på antibiotika.
exEn: The doctor wrote a prescription for antibiotics.
note: Also means 'recipe'. Receptfri medicin = over-the-counter medicine.

exEn: Have you taken your medicine today?
note: c before i is said like s. Ta medicin = to take medicine.

ex: Ta en {tablett} tre gånger om dagen.
exEn: Take one pill three times a day.

ex: Ta en {värktablett} och lägg dig och vila.
exEn: Take a painkiller and lie down and rest.
note: Many Swedes just say the brand names Alvedon or Ipren.

ex: Har du ett {plåster}? Jag har skurit mig.
exEn: Do you have a Band-Aid? I've cut myself.
note: The e drops out in plåstret and plåstren.

exEn: I've been vaccinated against the flu.
note: cc is said ks: vak-SIN. Vaccinera sig = to get vaccinated.

exEn: You need to rest for a few days.

ex: Det finns inget som kan {bota} en förkylning.
exEn: There's nothing that can cure a cold.

ex: Jag har nästan ingen {fritid} just nu.
exEn: I have almost no free time right now.
note: på fritiden = in your free time.

en: what do you do in your free time?
alt: what do you do in your spare time?
what do you do for fun?
ex: – {Vad gör du på fritiden?} – Jag spelar mest fotboll.
exEn: – What do you do in your free time? – Mostly I play soccer.
note: gör is pronounced jör. A common reply: Jag håller på med … (I do …).

exEn: Do you have a hobby?
note: Plural hobbyer: Vilka hobbyer har du?

exEn: We have the same interests.
note: Vad har du för intressen? = What are your interests? Interest on a loan is ränta.

exEn: Are you interested in sports?
note: intresserad av = interested in (av, not i).

ex: På helgerna vill jag bara {koppla av}.
exEn: On weekends I just want to relax.
note: The stress is on av.

exEn: I hang out with my cousins a lot.
note: Ends in -s in every form: umgås, umgicks, har umgåtts. umgås med = to spend time with.

alt: to go out on the town
ex: Ska vi {gå ut} och äta i kväll?
exEn: Shall we go out to eat tonight?
note: Also literally to go outside: Gå ut och lek! Irregular: gick ut, har gått ut.

exEn: We went to the movies last Saturday.
note: No article: gå på bio, not på en bio.

exEn: We're going to a party on Saturday.
note: ha fest = to throw a party; gå på fest = to go to a party. A political party is ett parti.

exEn: Shall we go for a walk?
note: ta en promenad or gå en promenad = to go for a walk.

exEn: We went on a day trip to the archipelago.
Which sport do you like best?
note: sporten can also mean the sports news on TV or radio.

exEn: We have PE on Fridays.
note: A more formal word than sport. At school (idrott och hälsa) it means PE.

ex: Jag försöker {träna} tre gånger i veckan.
exEn: I try to work out three times a week.
note: Also to coach: Hon tränar ett fotbollslag.

exEn: Practice starts at six.
I go to the gym after work.
note: g before y is soft: it sounds like jym. Same form in the plural: ett gym, två gym.

ex: Hon har spelat {fotboll} sedan hon var sex.
exEn: She has played soccer since she was six.
note: Also the ball itself: en fotboll, två fotbollar.

ex: Pappa tittar alltid på {ishockey} på tv.
exEn: Dad always watches ice hockey on TV.
note: Usually just hockey in everyday speech.

exEn: Sweden is good at handball.
note: Very popular in Sweden, both to play and to watch.

exEn: He's tall and plays basketball.
note: False friend: a basket is en korg.

exEn: Shall we play tennis on Sunday?
Can you swim?
note: simma is the act of swimming. Going for a swim for fun is usually bada.

en: to go for a swim; to bathe
exEn: Shall we go for a swim in the lake?
note: Means taking a dip in the sea or a lake, or having a bath. Swimming laps is simma.

exEn: I jog in the woods in the mornings.
note: springa is the everyday word for running: Jag springer fem kilometer.

exEn: I bike to work every day.
note: c is pronounced s: sykla.

ex: Vi ska {åka skidor} i Åre på sportlovet.
exEn: We're going skiing in Åre during the winter break.
note: sk before i sounds like sj. One ski is en skida. Sportlovet is a week off school in late winter.

exEn: The kids are skating on the lake.
note: The d is silent: skrisskor. One skate is en skridsko.

ex: Min dotter {rider} två gånger i veckan.
exEn: My daughter goes riding twice a week.
note: Irregular: rider, red, har ridit. Only for horses; bikes take cykla or åka.

exEn: Who won the game yesterday?
Which team do you support?
note: hålla på ett lag = to support a team. Don't mix it up with en lag (a law).

ex: Ett fotbollslag har elva {spelare} på planen.
exEn: A soccer team has eleven players on the field.
note: Same form in the plural: en spelare, två spelare.

exEn: The coach was pleased after the game.
note: Also a fitness trainer at the gym.

exEn: Throw the ball to me!
She scored two goals in the game.
note: göra mål = to score. Also a goal in life: Mitt mål är att lära mig svenska.

exEn: The team got three points.
note: Same form in the plural: en poäng, tre poäng. Also the point of something: Jag förstår inte poängen.

exEn: She won the competition!

alt: to take part in a competition
exEn: He competes in cross-country skiing.
note: tävla mot någon = to compete against someone.

exEn: Which team won?
note: Irregular: vinner, vann, har vunnit.

exEn: We lost the game by one goal.
note: To lose a thing like your keys is usually tappa bort: Jag har tappat bort nycklarna.

exEn: The game ended in a 1–1 draw.
note: Det blev oavgjort = It was a draw. Literally: undecided.

exEn: The winner gets a gold medal.
note: segrare means the same but is more formal, as in news reports.

exEn: Everyone cheered her on.
note: heja på = to cheer for. Also shouted at games: Heja Sverige! (Go Sweden!)

exEn: This game is so much fun!
note: Same form in the plural: ett spel, två spel. A sports game is usually en match.

exEn: Shall we play a board game?
note: spela kort = to play cards.

exEn: My son plays computer games all evening.
note: Console games are often called tv-spel.

ex: Morfar och jag brukar {fiska} vid sjön.
exEn: Grandpa and I usually fish by the lake.

ex: Vi ska {vandra} i fjällen i sommar.
exEn: We're going hiking in the mountains this summer.

ex: Vi {campade} vid en sjö i helgen.
exEn: We camped by a lake over the weekend.
note: c is pronounced k here: kampa. Sleeping in a tent is also tälta.

exEn: She sings in a choir.
note: Irregular: sjunger, sjöng, har sjungit.

exEn: Do you want to dance?
She paints pictures in her free time.
note: Also walls and houses: Vi ska måla om köket.

exEn: The kids are sitting and drawing.
note: rita = with a pen or pencil; måla = with paint.

exEn: He likes photographing birds.
note: In everyday speech often fota or ta bilder.

exEn: Grandma knits mittens for all the grandkids.
note: sticka also means to prick or sting, with other forms: sticker, stack, stuckit. In speech, Jag sticker nu = I'm off now.

exEn: Did you forget to turn off the stove?
note: En öppen spis is a fireplace.

exEn: Set the oven to 200 degrees.
note: g before n sounds like ng: "ungn".

ex: Kör den i {mikron} i två minuter.
exEn: Put it in the microwave for two minutes.
note: Everyday short form of mikrovågsugn.

exEn: The milk is in the fridge.
note: Often just kylen: Lägg det i kylen. k before y is soft (tj-sound).

exEn: There's ice cream in the freezer.
note: Related verb: frysa (to freeze). Jag fryser = I'm cold.

exEn: Can you empty the dishwasher?
Put the dirty dishes in the sink.
note: Also called diskho. A bathroom sink is a handfat.

exEn: We've bought a new coffee maker.
note: Like most -are words, the plural is the same: två kaffebryggare.

exEn: Should I put the kettle on?
note: Literally "water boiler".

exEn: I'm making toast in the toaster.
note: Toast is rostat bröd (toasted bread).

exEn: Boil water in a large saucepan.
note: Stress on the second syllable: kas-TRULL.

ex: Hetta upp lite olja i en {stekpanna}.
exEn: Heat a little oil in a frying pan.
note: Often just pannan in everyday speech.

ex: Lägg på ett {lock}, så kokar vattnet snabbare.
exEn: Put a lid on, and the water will boil faster.
note: False friend: a lock (for a door) is ett lås.

exEn: This knife is really sharp.
note: Unlike in English, the k is pronounced: k-niv.

exEn: Can I have a clean fork?
note: The plural drops the e: gafflar.

exEn: You eat soup with a spoon.
note: sk before e is the sj-sound.

ex: Jag tar en {tesked} socker i teet.
exEn: I take a teaspoon of sugar in my tea.
note: Written tsk in recipes.

exEn: Two tablespoons of sugar is enough.
note: Written msk in recipes.

exEn: The silverware is in the top drawer.
note: Knives, forks and spoons together. Stress on -stick.

ex: Ta en {tallrik} och ta för dig!
exEn: Grab a plate and help yourself!
Can I have a glass of water?
note: Same form in the plural: två glas. Don't mix it up with glass, which means ice cream!

exEn: Would you like a cup of coffee?
note: No word for "of": en kopp te = a cup of tea.

ex: Jag dricker te ur en stor {mugg}.
exEn: I drink tea from a big mug.
note: You drink ur (out of) a cup or mug.

exEn: Get out a big bowl.
note: Skål! on its own means Cheers!

ex: Hämta en {skärbräda} och en vass kniv.
exEn: Get a cutting board and a sharp knife.
note: From skära (to cut) + bräda (board).

exEn: Who does the cooking at your house?
note: Laga alone can also mean to fix: laga cykeln = to fix the bike.

exEn: Boil the potatoes for twenty minutes.
note: Also used for coffee: koka kaffe = to make coffee.

exEn: Fry the meatballs in butter.
note: Also used for roasting meat in the oven.

exEn: We baked cinnamon buns over the weekend.
Should we have a barbecue tonight?
He cut the tomatoes into pieces.
note: Irregular: skär, skar, skurit. sk before ä is the sj-sound.

exEn: Chop the onion finely.
Can you peel the potatoes?
note: Ett skal is a peel or shell.

exEn: Keep stirring the sauce.
note: Röra om = to give it a stir. Rör inte! = Don't touch!

ex: {Blanda} mjöl och socker i en skål.
exEn: Mix the flour and sugar in a bowl.
Can you whip the cream?
note: The tool is en visp (a whisk).

exEn: This tastes really good!
note: Vill du smaka? = Would you like a taste?

exEn: I'm heating up some soup for lunch.
Pour the milk into a saucepan.
note: Hälla upp = to pour a drink: Ska jag hälla upp kaffe?

exEn: Whose turn is it to do the dishes?
note: The dirty dishes are disken: Jag tar disken = I'll do the dishes.

ex: Kan du {duka}? Maten är snart klar.
exEn: Can you set the table? The food's almost ready.
note: From en duk (a tablecloth).

ex: Kan du hjälpa mig att {duka av}?
exEn: Can you help me clear the table?
note: The stress is on av.

exEn: What ingredients do we need?
note: Stress on the last syllable: ingredi-ENS.

exEn: What spices have you put in the stew?
note: Also a verb: krydda (kryddar) = to season.

exEn: You need three deciliters of milk.
note: Swedish recipes use dl: 1 dl = 100 ml, a little under half a cup.

exEn: Bring a liter of water to a boil.
note: Same form in the plural: två liter.

exEn: A pack of butter is 500 grams.
note: Same form in the plural: 200 gram.

exEn: The chicken is still raw inside.
note: Ett-form rått: rått kött = raw meat.

exEn: We're having boiled potatoes with the fish.
note: From koka. Kokt potatis is a classic Swedish side dish.

ex: Jag vill ha ett {stekt} ägg, tack.
exEn: I'd like a fried egg, please.
note: From steka.

ex: Det är en härlig {känsla} att vara hemma igen.
exEn: It's a wonderful feeling to be home again.
note: Jag har en känsla av att … = I have a feeling that …

ex: Jag {känner mig} hemma i Sverige nu.
exEn: I feel at home in Sweden now.
note: sig changes with the person: jag känner mig, du känner dig. Känn dig som hemma! = Make yourself at home!

ex: Jag är så {glad} att du kom!
exEn: I'm so happy you came!
note: The everyday word for happy. Neuter: glatt.

exEn: She was sad when the cat died.
note: The d is silent: 'lessen'. Jag är ledsen can also mean I'm sorry.

exEn: Mom gets angry when we fight.
note: -rg is pronounced 'rj'. arg på någon = angry with someone.

exEn: I'm afraid of spiders.
note: rädd för = afraid of. The neuter form rätt is rare.

ex: Och så levde de {lyckliga} i alla sina dagar.
exEn: And they lived happily ever after.
note: Deeper and more lasting than glad. False friend: it doesn't mean lucky (that's ha tur).

ex: Han var {olycklig} på sitt gamla jobb.
exEn: He was unhappy at his old job.
note: The prefix o- often means un-: olycklig, otålig, oärlig.

exEn: Are you happy with the food?
note: nöjd med = happy with. Opposite: missnöjd (dissatisfied).

ex: Min pappa är en väldigt {lugn} person.
exEn: My dad is a very calm person.
note: gn is pronounced 'ngn'. Ta det lugnt! = Take it easy!

ex: Jag är alltid {nervös} innan ett prov.
exEn: I'm always nervous before a test.

ex: Hon är väldigt {stressad} på jobbet just nu.
exEn: She's really stressed at work right now.
note: The verb stressa also means to rush: Stressa inte! = Take your time!

ex: Jag blir {orolig} när du inte svarar.
exEn: I get worried when you don't answer.
note: orolig för = worried about. The noun is oro (worry).

ex: Jag blir {irriterad} när folk kommer för sent.
exEn: I get annoyed when people are late.
note: The verb is irritera: Det irriterar mig = It annoys me.

exEn: I'm a bit disappointed with the result.
note: besviken på = disappointed in/with. Plural: besvikna.

ex: Jag blev {förvånad} när jag såg priset.
exEn: I was surprised when I saw the price.

ex: Barnen är {uttråkade} och vill gå hem.
exEn: The kids are bored and want to go home.
note: Don't mix them up: Jag är uttråkad = I'm bored, but Jag är tråkig = I'm boring!

exEn: I feel lonely sometimes.
note: Means both alone and lonely: Hon bor ensam. Plural doubles the m: ensamma.

ex: Jag tror att jag är {kär} i dig.
exEn: I think I'm in love with you.
note: kär i = in love with; bli kär = to fall in love. Also 'dear': Kära Anna (in letters).

exEn: We're so proud of you!
note: stolt över = proud of.

ex: Jag är väldigt {tacksam} för din hjälp.
exEn: I'm very grateful for your help.
note: tacksam för = grateful for. Plural doubles the m: tacksamma.

ex: Jag är så {avundsjuk} på din semester!
exEn: I'm so jealous of your vacation!
note: avundsjuk på = jealous of. Jealousy in a relationship is svartsjuk.

ex: Jag blev så {generad} när jag ramlade.
exEn: I was so embarrassed when I fell over.
note: From French gêné, so the g is pronounced like sj.

exEn: She's in a bad mood today.
note: False friend: humör means mood (the Swedish for humor is humor). på bra/dåligt humör = in a good/bad mood.

exEn: She cried with joy.
note: The noun of glad. No plural.

exEn: Love is the most important thing in life.
note: The verb is älska. Mostly uncountable, but en stor kärlek = a great love.

ex: Det var en stor {sorg} när mormor dog.
exEn: It was a great sorrow when Grandma died.
note: -rg is pronounced 'rj': sorj.

ex: Hon var röd i ansiktet av {ilska}.
exEn: She was red in the face with anger.
note: The adjective is arg.

ex: Min största {rädsla} är att bli ensam.
exEn: My biggest fear is being alone.
note: rädsla för = fear of. The adjective is rädd.

exEn: We laughed all evening.
note: skratta åt = to laugh at. The noun is ett skratt (a laugh).

exEn: She smiled at me.
note: Irregular: ler, log, lett. le mot = to smile at. The noun is ett leende (a smile).

exEn: The baby cried all night.
note: Irregular: grät, gråtit.

exEn: Don't worry, it'll work out.
note: oroa sig för = to worry about. sig changes with the person: jag oroar mig, du oroar dig.

exEn: I'm ashamed of what I said.
note: Ends in -s in every form: skäms, skämdes, skämts. Skäms på dig! = Shame on you!

exEn: I can't wait for summer!
note: längta efter = to long for; längta till = can't wait for; längta hem = to be homesick.

exEn: I miss you so much!
note: Missing a bus is missa; missing a person or place is sakna.

ex: Vi {trivs} jättebra i vår nya lägenhet.
exEn: We really like it in our new apartment.
note: Ends in -s in every form: trivs, trivdes, trivts. trivas med = to get on well with: Jag trivs med mina kollegor.

exEn: I care about you.
note: Very common in the negative: Jag bryr mig inte = I don't care.

exEn: I hate waiting.
note: The opposite of älska. The noun is ett hat (hatred).

exEn: That's so kind of you!
note: To children it means well-behaved: Var snäll nu!

ex: Var inte så {elak} mot din bror!
exEn: Don't be so mean to your brother!
note: elak mot någon = mean to someone.

ex: Var {ärlig} nu, gillar du min tröja?
exEn: Be honest, do you like my sweater?
note: Ärligt talat = to be honest, honestly.

exEn: He's a bit shy at first.

ex: Han är väldigt {social} och älskar fester.
exEn: He's very sociable and loves parties.
You were so brave at the dentist!

ex: Han är för {feg} för att säga sanningen.
exEn: He's too cowardly to tell the truth.
I've been lazy all weekend.
note: Neuter with double t: latt.

exEn: She's a very hard-working student.
note: The opposite of lat.

exEn: You're so good at Swedish!
note: duktig på = good at. Used about people; for things, say bra.

ex: Hon är {smart} och lär sig snabbt.
exEn: She's smart and learns quickly.

ex: Det var {dumt} av mig att säga så.
exEn: It was stupid of me to say that.
note: Children also use it for mean: Du är dum!

ex: Min dotter är lika {envis} som jag.
exEn: My daughter is as stubborn as I am.

ex: Man måste vara {tålmodig} med små barn.
exEn: You have to be patient with small children.
note: Opposite: otålig (impatient). A patient at the doctor's is en patient.

exEn: Our neighbors are very helpful.
note: hj is pronounced j: the h is silent.

exEn: Tell me about your weekend!
note: Stress on the second syllable: be-RÄT-ta. berätta om = tell about. To just say something is säga.

exEn: Can I ask you something?
note: To ask for something is be om: Hon bad om hjälp. The noun is en fråga (a question).

exEn: She asked me to wait outside.
note: Irregular: ber, bad, bett. be om = ask for: be om hjälp. Jag ber om ursäkt = I apologize. Also: to pray.

exEn: She's not answering her phone.
note: svara på = answer: svara på en fråga. The noun is ett svar (an answer).

exEn: Can you explain what it means?
note: Stress on -kla-: för-KLA-ra. The noun is en förklaring (an explanation).

exEn: Can you describe the man you saw?
note: Irregular like skriva: beskrev, beskrivit. The noun is en beskrivning (a description).

exEn: Could you repeat the question, please?
note: Stress on upp-. In everyday speech people often just say: Kan du säga det igen?

exEn: Someone called out my name.
note: ropa = call out loudly to get attention; skrika = scream or yell. ropa på hjälp = shout for help.

exEn: You don't have to shout!
note: Irregular: skrek, skrikit. A baby crying loudly also skriker.

exEn: She whispered something in my ear.
What do you mean?
note: A person menar (means, intends) something; a word betyder something: Vad betyder ordet?

exEn: What does this word mean?
note: Stress on -ty-. Past betydde, supine betytt. Du betyder mycket för mig = You mean a lot to me.

exEn: I promise to call tomorrow.
note: Jag lovar! = I promise! The noun is ett löfte (a promise).

exEn: He lied to his boss.
note: lj sounds like j: "juga". Irregular: ljög, ljugit. ljuga för = lie to. Lying in bed is ligga.

exEn: I'll call you after work.
note: ringa till någon = call someone. Det ringer på dörren = Someone is ringing the doorbell.

exEn: Can you send me the pictures?
note: sk before i sounds like sj. At the table: Kan du skicka saltet? = Can you pass the salt?

exEn: What are you thinking about?
note: tänka på = think about. Jag tänker åka hem = I intend to go home. Opinions use tycka; guesses use tro.

exEn: I think she's at home.
note: For things you're not sure about: Jag tror det = I think so. tro på = believe in. Opinions use tycka.

exEn: I wonder if the store is open.
note: A polite way to ask: Jag undrar om … = I was wondering if …

exEn: I hope you're feeling better.
note: Ends in -s in every form: hoppas, hoppades, hoppats. Hoppas det! = I hope so! Not to be confused with hoppa (to jump).

exEn: Remember to buy milk!
note: The everyday word for remember. Stress on ihåg. Jag kommer inte ihåg = I don't remember.

exEn: Do you remember when we met?
note: Ends in -s: minns, mindes, mints. Like komma ihåg, but more about memories of the past.

exEn: I forgot my jacket at your place.
note: glömma bort = forget completely. Glöm det! = Forget it!

exEn: I recognized her right away.
note: Stress on igen. k before ä is soft: tj-sound. Känner du igen mig? = Do you recognize me?

ex: Jag {märkte} inte att du kom in.
exEn: I didn't notice you came in.
note: Also: to mark (with a label). Det märks = It shows / You can tell.

exEn: Guess who I ran into today!
note: g before i is soft: "jissa".

exEn: We compared prices in different stores.
note: Present is jämför (like gör, kör). jämföra med = compare with.

exEn: You get to pick the movie tonight.
note: Irregular: valde, valt. An election is ett val.

ex: Vi {bestämde} oss för att stanna hemma.
exEn: We decided to stay home.
note: bestämma sig (för) = make up your mind: Har du bestämt dig? The formal word is besluta.

exEn: We're planning a trip to Norway.
note: Verbs ending in -era are stressed on the e: pla-NE-ra.

exEn: I'll try to be on time.
note: rs merges into one sh-like sound: fö-SHÖ-ka. Försök igen! = Try again! The noun is ett försök (an attempt).

exEn: Did you manage to find the keys?
note: Ends in -s in every form: lyckas, lyckades, lyckats. Lycka till! = Good luck!

exEn: It's okay if you fail.
note: Ends in -s in every form. Failing a test is usually: Jag klarade inte provet.

exEn: He seems nice.
note: Very common: Det verkar så = It seems so. Hon verkar trött = She seems tired.

exEn: Sounds good!
note: Two meanings: to sound (Det låter kul!) and to let (Låt mig hjälpa dig). Irregular: lät, låtit.

exEn: She got angry at me.
note: Irregular: blev, blivit. Often about the future: Det blir bra = It will be fine.

exEn: We've changed our plans.
note: ändra sig = change your mind: Jag har ändrat mig. Changing trains or clothes is byta.

exEn: I'm meeting Anna on Saturday.
note: träffas = meet each other: Ska vi träffas? Trevligt att träffas! = Nice to meet you! Also: to hit (a target).

exEn: I'll meet you at the station.
note: möta = meet someone arriving or coming toward you; spending time with someone is träffa. Also: to face (a problem).

exEn: We're waiting for the bus.
note: vänta på = wait for. Vänta lite! = Wait a moment! Vi väntar barn = We're expecting a baby.

exEn: Can you show me the way?
note: visa sig = turn out: Det visade sig att han ljög = It turned out he was lying.

en: to come along; to go along
exEn: Do you want to come along to the movies?
note: Stress on med. Följ med! = Come along! följa on its own = to follow.

ex: Jag {sprang} för att hinna med bussen.
exEn: I ran to catch the bus.
note: Irregular: sprang, sprungit. False friend: the season spring is vår.

exEn: The kids are jumping into the water.
note: hoppa över = skip: Jag hoppar över frukosten. Not to be confused with hoppas (to hope).

exEn: We have to hurry!
note: sk before y sounds like sj. sig changes with the person: jag skyndar mig, vi skyndar oss. Skynda dig! = Hurry up!

exEn: We're staying home tonight.
note: Two meanings: stay, and stop moving (Bussen stannar här). To stop doing something is sluta.

exEn: Keep going straight to the roundabout.
note: Forms like sätta: fortsatte, fortsatt. Fortsätt så! = Keep it up!

exEn: We have to turn around, the road is closed.
note: vända sig om = turn around (your body). Turning left or right on the road is svänga.

exEn: The leaves fall in autumn.
note: Irregular: föll, fallit. When people fall over, Swedes usually say ramla: Hon ramlade på isen.

exEn: We moved to Sweden last year.
note: For moving home and moving things: Kan du flytta bilen? Moving your body is röra sig.

exEn: Please have a seat!
note: sätta sig = sit down (the movement); sitta = be sitting. jag sätter mig, du sätter dig.

exEn: I'm going to lie down for a while.
note: lägga sig = lie down (the movement), also go to bed; ligga = be lying. Past also written lade sig.

en: to stand up; to get up
ex: Alla {reste sig} när hon kom in.
exEn: Everyone stood up when she came in.
note: From sitting or lying. Not the same as resa (to travel). Getting out of bed is stiga upp.

exEn: Put the keys on the table.
note: lägga = put something down flat; ställa = put upright; sätta = put in place. Past la (also written lade), lagt.

exEn: Put the milk in the fridge.
note: For things that stand upright. ställa en fråga = ask a question. ställa sig = go and stand somewhere.

exEn: I put a note on the door.
note: Supine satt looks like the past of sitta. sätta på = turn on: Sätt på tv:n!

exEn: You can hang your jacket in the hall.
note: hänga med = come along, or keep up: Hänger du med? = Are you coming? / Are you following?

exEn: I pick up the kids at preschool.
note: Go and get someone or something: Kan du hämta en stol? The opposite is lämna (drop off).

exEn: I left the keys with the neighbor.
note: lämna in = hand in. Simply going away is usually gå or åka: Jag måste gå nu.

exEn: Don't forget to bring an umbrella!
note: Stress on med. Often with a reflexive: Jag tar med mig mat = I'm bringing food.

ex: Kan du hjälpa mig att {bära} väskan?
exEn: Can you help me carry the bag?
note: Irregular: bär, bar, burit. Don't confuse bär (carries) with ett bär (a berry).

exEn: She held the child by the hand.
note: Irregular: höll, hållit. hålla med = agree; hålla på med = be busy with: Vad håller du på med?

exEn: Throw me the ball!
note: Also to throw away: Kasta inte maten! Slänga means the same.

exEn: The dog caught the ball.
note: To catch a bus is hinna med bussen; to catch a cold is bli förkyld.

exEn: I dropped my phone on the floor.
note: tappa bort = lose, misplace: Jag har tappat bort nyckeln. Losing a game is förlora.

exEn: You need to pull, not push!
note: Irregular: drog, dragit. Signs on doors: DRAG = pull, TRYCK = push.

exEn: Press the green button.
note: trycka på = press (a button). Doors say TRYCK = push. Also: to print.

exEn: The milk is in the fridge.
note: Cities and countries take i: i Sverige. With time it can mean 'for': i två år (for two years).

exEn: The book is on the table.
note: Also used for many places and events: på jobbet (at work), på bio (at the movies), på svenska (in Swedish).

exEn: We're going to Gothenburg tomorrow.
note: Also for whom something is meant: en present till dig (a present for you).

exEn: The train from Malmö is delayed.
I drink coffee with milk.
note: The d is often silent: 'me'. With transport it means 'by': med tåg (by train).

ex: Jag vill ha en kaffe {och} en kanelbulle.
exEn: I'd like a coffee and a cinnamon bun.
note: Usually pronounced 'å' in speech.

ex: Det är kallt ute, {men} solen skiner.
exEn: It's cold outside, but the sun is shining.
Would you like tea or coffee?
note: antingen … eller = either … or.

exEn: It's not that cold today.
note: In a main clause inte comes right after the verb: Jag förstår inte.

exEn: I want to come along too!
note: Often pronounced 'åså'. In writing you'll also see även (also; even).

exEn: Is anyone sitting here?
note: With movement use hit: Kom hit! (Come here!)

exEn: We lived there for five years.
note: With movement use dit: Vi åker dit imorgon. (We're going there tomorrow.)

exEn: I'm going home now. Bye!
note: For movement: Jag åker hem. Being at home is hemma.

exEn: I'm at home all day tomorrow.
note: For location. Going home is hem: Jag går hem.

exEn: It only takes five minutes.
She's always late.
note: The d is often silent: 'allti'.

exEn: I've never been to Kiruna.
note: The g is usually silent: 'aldri'.

exEn: We often eat fish on Fridays.
I sometimes take the bus to work.
note: Stressed on the second syllable: i-BLAND.

exEn: Maybe I'll come a bit later.
note: sk before e is the sj-sound: 'kan-sje'.

exEn: I'm working a lot right now.
note: 'Very' before adjectives (mycket bra), 'a lot, much' with verbs and nouns (mycket mat). The t is silent.

exEn: Would you like a little more coffee?
note: Also 'a bit' before adjectives: lite trött (a bit tired).

exEn: The movie was pretty good.
note: Weaker than it may sound: ganska bra ≈ pretty good, not great.

exEn: The food was really good!
note: The g is silent: 'väldit'. Very common in speech, like mycket before adjectives.

exEn: The shoes are too small.
note: för + adjective = too: för dyr (too expensive). 'Too' meaning 'also' is också.

exEn: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
note: Also 'during': under sommaren (during the summer).

exEn: The lamp hangs over the table.
note: Also 'past' with clock times: kvart över tre (a quarter past three).

exEn: The bike is behind the house.
Let's meet in front of the station at three.
May I sit next to you?
note: The d in bred- is silent: 'brevid'.

exEn: One of my friends is a teacher.
note: Also 'by' for who made something: en bok av Astrid Lindgren. Often pronounced 'a'.

exEn: I paid 200 kronor for the ticket.
note: For gifts, Swedes usually say till: en present till dig (a present for you).

exEn: We talked about the movie all evening.
note: With time it means 'in': om en vecka (in a week).

exEn: He went out without a jacket.
I sat between Anna and Erik.
I hope you're feeling better.
note: Also the infinitive marker 'to' (att äta = to eat), then often pronounced 'å'.

exEn: Call me when you get there!
note: Also the question word: När kommer du? (When are you coming?)

exEn: Let me know if you need help.
note: Also 'whether': Jag vet inte om hon kommer. (I don't know if she's coming.)

ex: Jag stannar hemma idag {eftersom} jag är sjuk.
exEn: I'm staying home today because I'm sick.
note: In speech, för is common too: Jag stannar hemma, för jag är sjuk.

ex: Jag har en kompis {som} bor i Umeå.
exEn: I have a friend who lives in Umeå.
note: Used for both people and things. Also 'as, like': lika stor som (as big as).

exEn: Have you already eaten?
Are you still tired?
note: ännu can also mean 'still' or 'yet': ännu inte (not yet).

exEn: Can you say that again?
note: The g sounds like j, and the stress is on the last syllable: i-JENN.

exEn: I was only ten then.
note: Also 'then, in that case': Vi ses imorgon då! (See you tomorrow, then!)

ex: Först äter vi, {sedan} går vi på bio.
exEn: First we eat, then we go to the movies.
note: Often shortened to sen: Vi ses sen! (See you later!)

exEn: Come here and look!
note: For movement to this place. Being here is här.

exEn: How do you get there?
note: For movement to that place. Being there is där.

exEn: The children are playing outside in the snow.
note: For location. With movement use ut: Gå ut och lek! (Go out and play!)

exEn: It's nice and warm inside.
note: For location. With movement use in: Kom in! (Come in!)

exEn: My keys are gone!
note: For location. With movement use bort: kasta bort (throw away).

exEn: See you after work!

ex: Vi äter middag {hos} mormor på söndag.
exEn: We're having dinner at Grandma's on Sunday.
note: At someone's home or workplace: hos tandläkaren (at the dentist's).

exEn: We walked through the park.
note: g before e is pronounced like j (English y): 'jeenom'.

exEn: We cycled around the lake.
note: Also 'about' with numbers: runt 100 personer (around 100 people).

exEn: Sweden is playing against Norway tonight.
note: Also 'toward': bussen mot centrum (the bus toward the city center).

exEn: It was raining, so we took the bus.
note: Also 'so' before adjectives: Det är så gott! (It's so good!)

exEn: He isn't Swedish but Norwegian.
note: After a negative, use utan (not men) for the right alternative: inte idag utan imorgon.

ex: Jag lyssnar på musik {medan} jag springer.
exEn: I listen to music while I run.
Wash your hands before you eat!
note: Before a noun you can also use före: före jul (before Christmas).

exEn: I'm calling to congratulate you.
note: In speech it can also mean 'because': Jag gick hem för att jag var trött.

exEn: My brother is older than me.
note: Also 'yet' in inte än (not yet).

ex: Jag har sovit dåligt, och {därför} är jag trött.
exEn: I slept badly, and that's why I'm tired.
note: därför att = because: Jag är trött därför att jag sov dåligt.

exEn: Shall we have lunch together?
note: Stressed on the second syllable: till-SAMM-ans.

exEn: Can we sit by the window?
note: For being right next to something: vid sjön (by the lake), vid bordet (at the table).

exEn: We've known each other since high school.
note: In speech usually shortened to sen.

exEn: But it's Saturday today, you know!
note: Points to something the listener already knows; often best left untranslated.

exEn: It'll probably be fine.
note: Also 'enough': Nog är nog! (Enough is enough!)

exEn: You're coming to the party, aren't you?
note: Invites agreement, like '…, right?' at the end of an English sentence.

exEn: Do you have a menu in English?
note: Stress on the last syllable: me-NY.

sv: Har ni ett bord för två?
en: do you have a table for two?
alt: do you have a table for 2
have you got a table for two
ipa: hɑːr niː ɛt ˈbuːɖ fœr ˈtvoː
ex: Hej! {Har ni ett bord för två} i kväll?
exEn: Hi! Do you have a table for two tonight?
note: Use ni (you, plural): you are asking the restaurant, not one person.

ex: Jag har {bokat bord} till klockan åtta.
exEn: I've booked a table for eight o'clock.
note: Usually said without an article: boka bord.

ex: Hej, jag har en {bokning} på namnet Ali.
exEn: Hi, I have a reservation under the name Ali.
note: Har ni bokat? = Do you have a reservation?

exEn: The waiter is bringing the food.
note: Stress on the last syllable. A waitress is a servitris.

ex: Min syster jobbar som {servitris} på ett kafé.
exEn: My sister works as a waitress at a café.
What can I get you today?
note: What staff say at the counter. Literally 'what may it be?'.

exEn: Can I have a glass of water?
note: The standard polite way to ask for something. Add tack at the end for extra politeness.

ex: {Jag skulle vilja ha} en kopp te, tack.
exEn: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
note: Polite and a little formal; Jag tar … is more everyday.

exEn: I'll have the same as her.
note: The usual way to order in Sweden: short, but not rude.

exEn: What do you want to order?
note: Don't mix it up with bestämma (to decide).

exEn: Our order hasn't come yet.
Which dish do you recommend?
note: Also an adjective: rätt = right, correct.

exEn: Would you like an appetizer?
note: Literally 'before dish'.

exEn: For the main course, I'll have the salmon.
note: Literally 'head dish'. A full dinner: förrätt, huvudrätt, efterrätt.

exEn: There's always room for dessert!
note: Literally 'after dish'. Swedish also has dessert, stressed on the last syllable.

exEn: The dish of the day is chicken with rice.
note: On weekdays many restaurants serve a cheap dagens lunch, often with salad and coffee included.

ex: {Portionerna} är stora på den här restaurangen.
exEn: The portions are big at this restaurant.
note: -tion is pronounced 'shoon'.

exEn: Shall we sit on the patio?
note: ute (outside) + servering (serving area). They fill up on the first warm day of spring.

ex: Vi {åt ute} på en thairestaurang igår.
exEn: We ate out at a Thai restaurant yesterday.
note: Irregular like äta: åt, ätit. It can also mean to eat outdoors.

exEn: We'll get takeout and eat at home.
note: From hämta (to pick up) + mat. Many people just say take away.

ex: – {Äta här eller ta med}? – Ta med, tack.
exEn: – For here or to go? – To go, please.
note: ta med = take with you. Also: Äter du här eller tar du med?

exEn: The food is ready. Enjoy your meal!
note: Said before eating, like bon appétit. The g in smaklig is silent.

exEn: Thanks for the meal, that was delicious!
note: gott is god (tasty) in the ett-form, agreeing with det.

ex: Jag kan inte äta mer, jag är {mätt}.
exEn: I can't eat any more, I'm full.
note: Don't say full about food: Jag är full means 'I'm drunk'!

exEn: Shall we split the bill?
note: Mostly heard in the definite form, notan.

exEn: We're done. The bill, please!
note: A little softer: Kan vi få notan?

exEn: We gave the waiter a small tip.
note: Uncountable: lite dricks. Tipping is optional in Sweden; many people just round up.

exEn: The coffee's on me today!
note: Irregular: bjöd, bjudit. Jag bjuder! = It's on me! bjuda in = to invite.

exEn: Cheers, and happy birthday!
note: Look people in the eye when you say skål. As a noun, en skål is a bowl.

ex: Jag är {vegetarian}, så jag äter inte kött.
exEn: I'm a vegetarian, so I don't eat meat.
note: No article after är: Jag är vegetarian.

exEn: Do you have anything vegetarian?
note: For a person, use the noun: Jag är vegetarian.

exEn: Are there any vegan options?
note: A vegan person is en vegan. The g is hard.

exEn: Do you have gluten-free bread?
note: -fri = -free: laktosfri, sockerfri, alkoholfri.

ex: Kan jag få {laktosfri} mjölk i kaffet?
exEn: Can I have lactose-free milk in my coffee?
I'm allergic to nuts.
note: allergic to = allergisk mot. The g is hard.

exEn: I feel like something sweet.
note: sugen på = craving, in the mood for. Also for activities: sugen på att bada.

ex: På jobbet har vi {fika} klockan tre.
exEn: At work we have our coffee break at three.
note: A Swedish institution: coffee or tea with something sweet, with friends or colleagues. Some say ett fika.

exEn: Shall we have coffee this afternoon?
We had coffee at a cozy pastry shop.
note: A traditional café that sells cakes and pastries. Stress on the last syllable.

exEn: Would you like a refill?
note: A second cup of coffee. In many cafés it is included: påtår ingår.

exEn: The whole house smells of cinnamon buns!
note: Stress on -nel-. October 4 is kanelbullens dag (Cinnamon Bun Day).

ex: Vill du ha en {kardemummabulle} eller en kanelbulle?
exEn: Do you want a cardamom bun or a cinnamon bun?
note: Stress on -mum-.

ex: Vi köpte en {tårta} till pappas födelsedag.
exEn: We bought a cake for Dad's birthday.
note: A tårta is a big cake with cream or filling, for celebrations; a kaka is a plain cake or a cookie.

ex: Mormor fyller år, så vi köper en {prinsesstårta}.
exEn: It's Grandma's birthday, so we're buying a princess cake.
note: Sponge cake with jam, custard and whipped cream under a dome of green marzipan.

ex: Hur många {semlor} har du ätit i år?
exEn: How many semlor have you eaten this year?
note: A cardamom bun filled with almond paste and whipped cream, eaten in late winter, above all on Shrove Tuesday (fettisdagen).

exEn: This Danish is still warm.
note: Literally 'Vienna bread'. The w is pronounced like v.

exEn: Shall we bake a sticky chocolate cake?
note: From kladdig (sticky, gooey). Often served with whipped cream.

ex: Barnen gör {chokladbollar} av havregryn och kakao.
exEn: The kids are making chocolate balls from oats and cocoa.
note: A no-bake treat of oats, sugar, butter and cocoa, often rolled in coconut.

exEn: My computer is so slow today.
note: The stress moves in the plural: datorer = da-TOO-rer. A laptop is a bärbar dator (or just laptop).

exEn: Call me on my cell phone.
note: Short for mobiltelefon. Stress on the last syllable: mo-BEEL.

exEn: The kids are watching a movie on the tablet.
note: False friend: en tablett is a pill, not a tablet computer.

exEn: The screen on my phone has cracked.
note: sk before ä is the sj-sound: "shärm".

ex: Mitt {tangentbord} har inte å, ä och ö.
exEn: My keyboard doesn't have å, ä and ö.
note: En tangent is a key on the keyboard.

ex: Det är slut på papper i {skrivaren}.
exEn: The printer is out of paper.
note: Like most -are words, the plural is the same: två skrivare.

exEn: Can I borrow your charger?
The battery is almost dead.
note: Stress on the last syllable: batte-RI.

exEn: Where are my headphones?
note: Usually plural. One earbud is en hörlur.

exEn: We don't have any internet at the cabin.
note: Usually used without an article: på internet = online.

exEn: I bought the tickets online.
note: Nätet = the internet: på nätet = online.

exEn: Do you have Wi-Fi here?
note: Pronounced "vaj-faj". Usually ett wifi, wifit; some say wifin.

exEn: I've forgotten my password.
note: lösen (watchword) + ord (word).

exEn: Enter your username and password.
note: användare (user) + namn (name).

exEn: You have to create an account first.
note: Also a bank account: bankkonto.

exEn: There's an app for that.
The opening hours are on our website.
note: In everyday speech any website is a hemsida. Also webbsida (web page) and the official webbplats.

exEn: Can you send me the link?

ex: Jag {sökte} på nätet men hittade ingenting.
exEn: I searched online but didn't find anything.
note: söka jobb = to apply for jobs. To google something is googla.

exEn: I got an email from my boss.
note: Also spelled mail. The formal word is e-post. Same form in the plural: två mejl.

exEn: I'll email you the address.
I'm attaching my CV.
note: En bifogad fil = an attachment.

ex: Jag skickar ett {sms} när jag är framme.
exEn: I'll send a text when I get there.
note: Said letter by letter: ess-emm-ESS. Same form in the plural: två sms.

exEn: Text me when you're home!
note: In casual speech also messa.

exEn: You have a new message.
note: Plural: meddelanden. From meddela (to inform).

exEn: I've quit social media.
note: Plural in Swedish: ett medium, flera medier.

exEn: I liked your post.
note: To post something is lägga upp: Hon la upp en bild.

ex: Hon {delade} inlägget med alla sina vänner.
exEn: She shared the post with all her friends.
note: Also to split: Vi delar på notan (We split the bill).

exEn: I'll send the file in an email.
note: fil also means a traffic lane, and the sour milk filmjölk is often just called fil.

exEn: The pictures are in this folder.
note: False friend: a map is en karta.

exEn: Send a picture of the cat!
note: Also any photo: ta en bild = to take a picture.

exEn: Have you seen the video I sent?
note: Plural videor, informally also videos.

exEn: You can download the app for free.
note: Also written ladda ned. The stress is on ner.

exEn: I'll upload the pictures tonight.
note: The stress is on upp.

exEn: I need to charge my phone.
note: Also to load: Sidan laddas (The page is loading).

exEn: I accidentally deleted all the pictures.
note: In everyday speech also ta bort (to remove).

exEn: Can you print the tickets?
note: Irregular like skriva: skrev ut, skrivit ut. The doctor skriver ut medicin = prescribes it.

exEn: Log in with BankID.
note: The stress is on in.

exEn: Remember to log out afterward.
Have you updated the app?

ex: Vi {installerade} ett nytt program på datorn.
exEn: We installed a new program on the computer.
Click the link in the email.
note: Use på: klicka på knappen = click the button.

exEn: The printer isn't working.
note: Only for things that function; a person who works arbetar or jobbar. Casual: funka.

en: to turn off; to switch off
exEn: Turn off your phone during the movie.
note: The opposite is sätta på or slå på (to turn on).

ex: Har du testat att {starta om} datorn?
exEn: Have you tried restarting the computer?
note: The stress is on om.

ex: Jag tror att datorn har fått ett {virus}.
exEn: I think the computer has a virus.
note: Same form in the plural: två virus.

exEn: Save a copy just in case.
note: för säkerhets skull = just in case, to be on the safe side.

exEn: Do you have BankID on your phone?
note: The electronic ID Swedes use to log in to banks and authorities, sign documents and pay. Said "bank-i-de".

exEn: Almost everything is digital now.
note: Stress on the last syllable: digi-TAL.

exEn: I want wireless headphones.
note: tråd (wire, thread) + -lös (-less). Trådlöst nätverk = wireless network.

ex: Det är svårt att hitta en {bostad} i Stockholm.
exEn: It's hard to find a place to live in Stockholm.
note: Plural with a vowel change: bostäder. Bostadsbrist = housing shortage.

exEn: How much is the rent?
note: Rent is normally paid in advance, before the month starts.

ex: Hon {hyr} ett rum hos en äldre dam.
exEn: She rents a room from an elderly lady.
note: Present tense hyr, not hyrer. Hyra ut = to rent out.

exEn: Contact the landlord if something breaks.
note: Often a housing company rather than a person. Värd = host.

exEn: The tenants got a letter from the landlord.
note: Gäst = guest; the g is soft, like j. Hyresgästföreningen is the tenants' union.

ex: Läs {hyreskontraktet} noga innan du skriver under.
exEn: Read the lease carefully before you sign.
note: Kontrakt is stressed on the second syllable: kon-TRAKT. A lease directly with the landlord is a förstahandskontrakt.

ex: Hon har bara ett {andrahandskontrakt} på lägenheten.
exEn: She only has a sublease on the apartment.
note: Hyra i andra hand = to sublet. The landlord usually has to approve it.

exEn: Do you live in a rental or a co-op apartment?
note: An apartment you rent and can't sell. Compare bostadsrätt, which you buy.

exEn: They bought a co-op apartment in Södermalm.
note: You buy the right to live there and pay a monthly fee (avgift) to the housing association.

ex: De bor i en {villa} med stor trädgård.
exEn: They live in a house with a big yard.
note: False friend: a villa is any ordinary detached house, not a luxury home.

ex: Vi har köpt ett {radhus} utanför stan.
exEn: We've bought a townhouse outside town.
note: Rad = row. Same form in the plural: två radhus.

exEn: The apartment is sixty square meters.
note: Written kvm or m² in housing ads. Same form in the plural: sextio kvadratmeter.

ex: Jag har stått i {bostadskön} i fem år.
exEn: I've been in the housing queue for five years.
note: In the big cities people often queue for many years to get a rental apartment.

ex: Kan du hjälpa mig med {flytten} på lördag?
exEn: Can you help me with the move on Saturday?
note: The noun of flytta. Tell Skatteverket about a move with a flyttanmälan.

ex: Vi {flyttar in} i den nya lägenheten i maj.
exEn: We're moving into the new apartment in May.
note: The particle is stressed: flytta IN. Flytta ut = to move out; flytta ihop = to move in together.

exEn: We've packed twenty moving boxes.
note: Kartong = cardboard box. The rt merges into one retroflex sound.

exEn: The notice must be in writing.
note: Uppsägningstid = notice period, usually three months for a rental apartment. From säga upp.

exEn: Is electricity included in the rent?
note: Short for elektricitet. Elräkning = electricity bill.

exEn: The heating isn't working in the bedroom.
note: Also heat or warmth in general: solens värme.

exEn: Have you paid the bills?
note: At a restaurant you ask for notan, not räkningen.

exEn: The fee is four thousand kronor a month.
note: The g is soft, like j. In a bostadsrätt you pay a monthly avgift instead of rent.

exEn: Does the insurance pay for the damage?
note: Stress on the second syllable: för-SÄK-ring. The rs merges into one sh-like sound.

exEn: Everyone should have home insurance.
note: Covers your belongings and usually travel too. Almost every household in Sweden has one.

ex: Jag har bokat {tvättstugan} på torsdag kväll.
exEn: I've booked the laundry room for Thursday evening.
note: The shared laundry room in an apartment building. You book a time slot (tvättid) in advance.

exEn: The garbage room is in the courtyard.
note: The definite form doubles the m: soprummet.

exEn: Can you take out the trash?
note: Plural only in this sense. A garbage can is en soptunna.

exEn: Where can I throw away old batteries?
note: The everyday word for throwing things away. Kasta is to throw (a ball).

ex: Vi lämnar glas och tidningar på {återvinningen}.
exEn: We take glass and newspapers to the recycling station.
note: In everyday speech återvinningen often means the recycling station (återvinningsstation).

ex: Grannarna {stör} oss med hög musik varje helg.
exEn: The neighbors disturb us with loud music every weekend.
note: Present tense stör, not störer. Förlåt att jag stör! = Sorry to bother you!

exEn: What's your address?
note: Spelled with one d: adress.

exEn: Has the mail come yet?
note: Can also mean the postal service: skicka något med posten. Email is mejl.

ex: Det kom ett {brev} till dig idag.
exEn: A letter came for you today.
note: Same form in the plural: två brev. A letter of the alphabet is en bokstav.

ex: Jag ska hämta ut ett {paket} i affären.
exEn: I'm going to pick up a package at the store.
note: Stress on the second syllable: pa-KET. Hämta ut = to collect (a parcel).

ex: Jag fick en {avi} om att paketet har kommit.
exEn: I got a notice that the package has arrived.
note: Often a text message saying where to collect a parcel; bring ID. A hyresavi is a rent invoice.

exEn: Have you checked the mailbox today?
note: Both your own mailbox and the yellow public box for sending letters.

exEn: There's a signature missing on the form.
note: From skriva under (to sign). The rs merges into one sh-like sound.

ex: Du måste {skriva under} här och här.
exEn: You need to sign here and here.
note: The particle under is stressed. Skriva på means the same: skriva på kontraktet.

ex: Du kan ladda ner {blanketten} på hemsidan.
exEn: You can download the form from the website.
note: False friend: a blanket is en filt. An online form is usually called formulär.

en: to fill in; to fill out
exEn: Fill in your name and personal ID number.
note: The particle i is stressed and long: fyll I. Fylla alone means to fill.

ex: Man måste kontakta många {myndigheter} när man flyttar hit.
exEn: You have to contact lots of agencies when you move here.
note: Many agencies end in -verket or -kassan: Skatteverket, Migrationsverket, Försäkringskassan. The g is often silent.

exEn: Can I have your personal ID number?
note: Your date of birth plus four digits: YYMMDD-XXXX. You need it almost everywhere. Definite: personnumret.

exEn: Once you're registered, you get a personal ID number.
note: Registered at an address = folkbokförd, in everyday speech skriven: Var är du skriven?

exEn: Can I see your ID?
note: Usually shortened to leg: Har du leg? A passport, an ID card or a Swedish driver's license all count.

ex: Du kan beställa ett {id-kort} hos Skatteverket.
exEn: You can order an ID card from the Tax Agency.
note: Also written ID-kort. Skatteverket issues them to people registered (folkbokförda) in Sweden.

ex: Hyresvärden vill se att du har en fast {inkomst}.
exEn: The landlord wants to see that you have a steady income.
note: Many landlords ask for an income of about three times the rent.

ex: Hur mycket {skatt} betalar man i Sverige?
exEn: How much tax do you pay in Sweden?
note: Skatt also means treasure. Skatteverket = the Swedish Tax Agency.

ex: {Deklarationen} ska vara inne i början av maj.
exEn: The tax return is due at the beginning of May.
note: To file your tax return = deklarera. Most people just approve it online with BankID.

ex: Jag behöver ett {intyg} från min arbetsgivare.
exEn: I need a certificate from my employer.
note: Läkarintyg = doctor's certificate. Same form in the plural: två intyg.

exEn: She has been granted a residence permit in Sweden.
note: Issued by Migrationsverket. A permanent residence permit is often called PUT.

exEn: He has applied for Swedish citizenship.
note: A citizen is en medborgare. The g in -borgar- sounds like j.

exEn: How does Swedish society work?
note: Also a small town or village: ett litet samhälle.

exEn: Which country are you from?
note: Irregular plural: länder. På landet = in the countryside.

exEn: She has traveled all over the world.
note: The l is silent: rld is said as one retroflex d.

exEn: The state should pay for that.
note: Staten = the national level, as opposed to the kommun. Don't mix it up with en stad (a city).

exEn: Call the municipality and ask about preschool.
note: Sweden has 290 kommuner. They run schools, preschools and elderly care.

exEn: The region is responsible for health care.
note: Sweden's 21 regions (formerly called landsting) mainly run health care and public transport.

ex: Sverige har en {kung} och en drottning.
