exEn: Sweden has a king and a queen.
note: drottning = queen. The Swedish king has no political power.

exEn: The government wants to lower taxes.
note: The g is said like j: re-JE-ring.

exEn: Which parties are in parliament?
note: Sweden's parliament, usually in the definite and lowercase: riksdagen. It is elected every four years.

exEn: Who is Sweden's prime minister?
note: Plural statsministrar: the e drops. A minister = en minister.

exEn: Are you interested in politics?
note: Also 'policy': regeringens politik = the government's policy.

exEn: I don't trust politicians.
note: The stress moves: poLItiker, but poliTIK. Same form in the plural.

exEn: It's a political issue.
Which party are you going to vote for?
note: Only a political party. A party with friends is en fest.

exEn: Are you going to vote in the election?
note: rösta på ett parti = to vote for a party. Ett val = an election (en val is a whale).

exEn: Every vote counts.
note: Also 'voice': Hon har en fin röst.

exEn: All citizens over 18 have the right to vote.
note: Non-citizens living in Sweden can usually vote in municipal and regional elections, but not for the riksdag.

exEn: In a democracy, the people decide.
Did you see the debate on TV yesterday?

ex: Alla har rätt till sin egen {åsikt}.
exEn: Everyone has the right to their own opinion.
note: In everyday speech people often just ask: Vad tycker du?

ex: Det är {olagligt} att köra utan körkort.
exEn: It's illegal to drive without a license.
note: From en lag = a law (ett lag is a team). The opposite is laglig (legal).

exEn: Children have rights too.
note: mänskliga rättigheter = human rights.

exEn: We have both rights and obligations.
note: sky- has the sj-sound. skyldig = obliged; guilty; owing (money).

ex: Många kom hit för att leva i {frihet}.
exEn: Many people came here to live in freedom.

ex: Vi pratade om {jämställdhet} på SFI idag.
exEn: We talked about gender equality at SFI today.
note: Equality between women and men. Equality between people in general is jämlikhet.

exEn: The family is demanding justice.
note: The adjective rättvis means fair: Det är inte rättvist!

exEn: The company took the matter to court.
note: en dom = a verdict or sentence; en domare = a judge (also a referee).

exEn: The number of crimes has gone down this year.
note: Same form in the plural: ett brott, två brott. A criminal = en brottsling.

ex: Han dömdes till två år i {fängelse}.
exEn: He was sentenced to two years in prison.
Someone has stolen my bike!
note: Irregular: stjäl, stal, stulit. Stj is the sj-sound. A theft = en stöld.

exEn: You have to report the theft to the police.
note: anmäla sig = to sign up (for a course or a test).

exEn: The economy is growing slowly right now.
note: Also your own finances: Jag har dålig ekonomi = I'm short of money.

exEn: Unemployment is highest among young people.
note: Usually definite in Swedish: arbetslösheten ökar = unemployment is rising.

exEn: Are you a member of a union?
note: In everyday speech: facket (the union). Most employees in Sweden are members.

exEn: Taxes pay for the welfare system.
note: välfärden = schools, health care, elderly care and so on, paid for with taxes.

exEn: She works in health care.
note: vård = care: tandvård = dental care, äldrevård = elderly care.

exEn: She became a Swedish citizen last year.
note: medborgarskap = citizenship. The g in borg is said like j.

exEn: Gothenburg has about 600,000 inhabitants.
note: Same form in the plural: en invånare, två invånare.

exEn: Sweden's population is getting older and older.

ex: {Invandringen} var en stor fråga i valet.
exEn: Immigration was a big issue in the election.
Many immigrants study Swedish at SFI.
note: invandra = to immigrate; utvandra = to emigrate.

exEn: Language is the key to integration.
The family came to Sweden as refugees.
note: fly = to flee; flykt = escape.

ex: Jag tittar alltid på {nyheterna} på kvällen.
exEn: I always watch the news in the evening.
note: The news (on TV or radio) = nyheterna, plural. En nyhet = one piece of news.

exEn: I read about it in the paper.
note: Also a magazine. In everyday speech the d is often silent: 'tining'.

exEn: Have you read the article about the school?
note: Plural artiklar: the e drops.

exEn: My parents fled from the war.
note: Same form in the plural: ett krig, två krig.

exEn: Everyone wants to live in peace.
note: Lämna mig i fred! = Leave me alone!

exEn: During the crisis, many people lost their jobs.
note: Plural kriser (English: crises).

exEn: Thousands of people took part in the protests.
note: protestera = to protest. A protest march is usually called en demonstration.

exEn: The Red Cross is a big organization.
note: -tion is said 'shoon' and takes the stress.

ex: Det finns {föreningar} för nästan allt i Sverige.
exEn: There are clubs for almost everything in Sweden.
note: A non-profit club or society, e.g. idrottsförening = sports club.

exEn: We're following developments closely.
note: utveckla = to develop.

ex: Ny {forskning} visar att kaffe är nyttigt.
exEn: New research shows that coffee is good for you.
note: No plural, like English research. A researcher = en forskare.

exEn: She works for an international company.
Social media influences young people.
We need to think more about the environment.
note: Stress on the last syllable: mil-JÖ. It also means surroundings: arbetsmiljö = working environment.

ex: Tåget är ett {miljövänligt} sätt att resa.
exEn: The train is an eco-friendly way to travel.
The climate is getting warmer and warmer.
Climate change affects the whole world.
note: Usually plural in Swedish: klimatförändringarna = climate change.

exEn: We have to cut carbon dioxide emissions.
note: Same form in the plural: ett utsläpp, många utsläpp. From släppa ut (to let out).

exEn: Air pollution can cause asthma.
note: Mostly used in the plural. The verb is förorena (to pollute).

exEn: We use less energy in the summer.
note: Stress on the last syllable, and g before i sounds like sj: e-ner-SHEE.

exEn: Sweden is investing heavily in renewable energy.
note: The older word förnyelsebar means the same.

exEn: Solar energy is getting cheaper every year.

ex: Det byggs mycket {vindkraft} i norra Sverige.
exEn: A lot of wind power is being built in northern Sweden.
note: A wind turbine is ett vindkraftverk.

exEn: Coal and oil are fossil fuels.
note: fossila bränslen = fossil fuels.

exEn: We recycle glass, paper and plastic.
note: Irregular like vinna: återvann, återvunnit. The noun is återvinning (recycling).

ex: Det är {pant} på burkar och plastflaskor.
exEn: There's a deposit on cans and plastic bottles.
note: Usually 1 or 2 kronor. You get it back at the bottle machine in the supermarket (pantmaskinen).

exEn: I'm going to return the cans at the store.
note: The machine gives you a receipt (pantkvitto) that you use at the checkout.

ex: Hemma {sorterar} vi soporna i olika påsar.
exEn: At home we sort our trash into different bags.
note: Sorting household waste for recycling is called sopsortering or källsortering.

exEn: You can put food scraps in the compost.
note: Stress on the second syllable: kom-POST.

exEn: How do we build a sustainable society?
note: It also means durable: hållbara kläder. The noun is hållbarhet (sustainability).

exEn: I try to buy organic food.
note: Often shortened to eko: ekomjölk, ekobananer.

exEn: There was a lot of litter on the beach.
note: Also junk in general: Källaren är full av skräp.

ex: Det är förbjudet att {skräpa ner} i naturen.
exEn: It's forbidden to litter in nature.
note: Stress on ner. Also written skräpa ned.

ex: Det finns alldeles för mycket {plast} i haven.
exEn: There's far too much plastic in the oceans.
note: en plastpåse = a plastic bag.

exEn: Don't forget to rinse the packaging!
note: Packaging is recycled by material: plast, papper, glas or metall.

exEn: We shouldn't waste water.
note: Often slösa med: slösa med vatten, pengar, tid. The opposite is spara.

exEn: Turn off the light to save energy.
We have to protect the forest and the animals.
note: sk before y sounds like sj: SHYD-da. The noun is ett skydd (protection).

exEn: Many birds and insects are endangered.
note: utrotning (extinction) + hotad (threatened).

ex: {Allemansrätten} ger alla rätt att vara ute i naturen.
exEn: The right of public access gives everyone the right to be out in nature.
note: You may walk, camp for a night and pick berries almost anywhere. The rule: inte störa, inte förstöra (don't disturb, don't destroy). Always used in this definite form.

ex: Jag gillar {friluftsliv}, särskilt att vandra och fiska.
exEn: I like outdoor life, especially hiking and fishing.
note: A big part of Swedish life: spending free time out in nature, all year round.

exEn: Sarek is one of Sweden's national parks.
note: Sweden has about 30, from Abisko in the far north to Söderåsen in Skåne.

exEn: In the nature reserve, dogs must be on a leash.

ex: Långt upp i norr finns det mycket {vildmark}.
exEn: Far up north there's a lot of wilderness.

ex: Ön är känd för sitt rika {djurliv}.
exEn: The island is known for its rich wildlife.
note: dj- sounds like j: djur = YOOR.

exEn: Don't forget to water the plants!
note: From växa (to grow). A houseplant is en krukväxt.

ex: Vi ska vandra i {fjällen} i sommar.
exEn: We're going hiking in the mountains this summer.
note: fjällen = the bare mountains of northern and western Sweden, above the tree line. Berg is the general word for mountain.

exEn: We paddled a canoe on the river.
note: Used for the big rivers of northern Sweden, like Torne älv. Flod is mostly used for rivers abroad: Nilen är en flod.

exEn: Cloudberries grow on bogs up north.
note: Don't mix it up with myra (ant).

exEn: The glaciers melt as the climate gets warmer.
note: c before i sounds like s, and the stress is on the last syllable: gla-si-ÄR.

exEn: Kungsleden is Sweden's best-known hiking trail.
note: Often just leden: Följ leden! (Follow the trail!) Trails are marked with paint on trees and rocks.

exEn: Follow the path through the forest to the lake.
note: Also the imperative of stiga: Stig på! = Come in!

exEn: We slept in a tent by the lake.
note: The verb tälta means to camp in a tent.

ex: Ta med en varm {sovsäck}, nätterna är kalla.
exEn: Bring a warm sleeping bag, the nights are cold.

ex: Vi satt runt {elden} och grillade korv.
exEn: We sat around the fire and grilled sausages.
note: Eld is a fire you make, like in a fireplace; a fire that destroys a building is en brand. Göra upp eld = to make a fire.

exEn: We sang songs around the campfire.
Can you eat this mushroom?
note: It also means sponge. Many Swedes pick mushrooms in the autumn, especially kantareller (chanterelles).

exEn: We usually pick mushrooms in the autumn.
note: plocka upp = to pick up: Plocka upp ditt skräp!

exEn: The adder is Sweden's only venomous snake.
note: g before i sounds like j: YIF-tig. ett gift = a poison, but the adjective gift means married!

ex: Skogen är full av {bär} i augusti.
exEn: The forest is full of berries in August.
note: Same form in the plural: ett bär, två bär. Don't confuse it with bär (carries) from bära.

ex: Jag äter yoghurt med {blåbär} till frukost.
exEn: I have yogurt with blueberries for breakfast.
note: Wild Swedish blueberries (bilberries) are blue all the way through and stain your fingers.

ex: Vi äter köttbullar med potatis och {lingon}.
exEn: We're having meatballs with potatoes and lingonberries.
note: Usually eaten as lingonsylt (lingonberry jam) with meatballs, pancakes and much more.

ex: Hur {firar} man jul i ditt land?
exEn: How do people celebrate Christmas in your country?
The whole family was at the celebration.
note: Action nouns in -ande are ett-words: ett firande, ett leende.

ex: I vår familj är det {tradition} att baka lussekatter.
exEn: In our family, it's a tradition to bake saffron buns.
note: -tion is pronounced 'shoon', and it takes the stress.

exEn: Grandma always cooks traditional Swedish Christmas food.

ex: Jag vill lära mig mer om svensk {kultur}.
exEn: I want to learn more about Swedish culture.
Christmas is the biggest holiday of the year.
note: Usually pronounced 'höktid', with a short ö.

ex: – Är kaffet för varmt? – Nej, det är {lagom}.
exEn: – Is the coffee too hot? – No, it's just right.
note: A Swedish ideal: not too much, not too little. It never changes form: lagom stor, lagom varmt.

exEn: What a cozy café!
note: Also used about evenings and people: en mysig kväll. In everyday speech the g is often silent: 'mysi'.

ex: Vi {myser} i soffan med en film.
exEn: We're getting cozy on the sofa with a movie.
note: The noun is mys: Nu blir det mys! (Time to get cozy!)

ex: I kväll blir det {fredagsmys} med tacos och chips.
exEn: Tonight it's a cozy Friday night in with tacos and chips.
note: A Swedish ritual: snacks and TV on the sofa with the family. Fredag is usually pronounced 'freda'.

ex: Många menar att {jantelagen} lever kvar i Sverige.
exEn: Many people think the Law of Jante lives on in Sweden.
note: An unwritten rule: don't think you're better than anyone else. From a 1933 novel by Aksel Sandemose. Always used in this definite form.

ex: Första maj är en {röd dag}, så jag är ledig.
exEn: May Day is a public holiday, so I'm off work.
note: Public holidays are printed in red in Swedish calendars. Plural: röda dagar.

exEn: What are you doing for Christmas?
note: Holidays are written in lowercase: jul, påsk, midsommar. i jul = this Christmas.

ex: På {julafton} tittar vi på Kalle Anka klockan tre.
exEn: On Christmas Eve we watch Donald Duck at three o'clock.
note: The main day of the Swedish Christmas: the food, the presents and tomten all come on 24 December.

exEn: Merry Christmas, everyone!
note: god sounds like 'go'. Often followed by: och gott nytt år!

exEn: Santa brings presents on Christmas Eve.
note: Also the little gnome of folklore who guards the farm. The Swedish Santa knocks on the door in person!

exEn: What would you like for Christmas?
note: i julklapp = as a Christmas present: Jag fick en bok i julklapp.

exEn: The kids help decorate the Christmas tree.
note: klä granen = decorate the tree. Traditionally it comes down on 13 January (tjugondag Knut).

ex: Vi går på {julbord} med jobbet i december.
exEn: We're going to a Christmas buffet with work in December.
note: Herring, ham, meatballs and much more. Many workplaces book one for their staff.

exEn: The kids drink Christmas soda with the meal.
note: A dark, sweet soft drink sold mainly at Christmas. In December, Swedes drink more julmust than Coca-Cola.

exEn: There's alcohol-free mulled wine too.
note: Served hot in small cups with raisins and almonds, all through December.

exEn: Would you like mulled wine and gingerbread cookies?
note: Literally 'pepper cake'. Swedes joke that eating them makes you kind (snäll).

ex: På {lucia} äter vi lussekatter till frukost.
exEn: On Saint Lucy's Day we eat saffron buns for breakfast.
note: 13 December. Also the girl in white with candles in her hair who leads the procession: Hon är lucia i år.

ex: Min dotter är med i {luciatåget} på förskolan.
exEn: My daughter is in the Lucia procession at preschool.
note: tåg usually means 'train'; here it means 'procession'. Lucia leads, followed by maids, star boys and gingerbread men.

exEn: Shall we bake saffron buns this weekend?
note: An S-shaped saffron bun with raisins, eaten in December. Also called lussebulle.

exEn: We watch the fireworks on New Year's Eve.
note: Often just called nyår: Vad gör du på nyår?

exEn: It's twelve o'clock! Happy New Year!
note: gott and nytt end in -t because år is an ett-word.

ex: I {påsk} ska vi åka skidor i fjällen.
exEn: This Easter we're going skiing in the mountains.
note: Children dress up as påskkärringar (Easter witches) and go door to door for candy.

exEn: The kids are looking for the Easter eggs in the garden.
note: Often a big paper egg filled with candy rather than a chocolate egg.

ex: Vi har ett {påskris} med gula fjädrar i köket.
exEn: We have Easter twigs with yellow feathers in the kitchen.
note: Birch twigs in a vase, decorated with colorful feathers. Here ris means 'twigs', not 'rice'.

exEn: On Walpurgis Night people light big bonfires.
note: 30 April: bonfires and choir songs to welcome spring. Short for valborgsmässoafton.

exEn: I'm taking the bridge day off.
note: A workday squeezed (klämd) between a public holiday and a weekend. Many people take it off.

exEn: Sweden's national day is June 6.
note: A public holiday since 2005. Swedes celebrate it more quietly than many other countries do.

exEn: My little brother graduates from high school in June.
note: On the big day, graduates in white caps run out of school (springer ut) to families holding signs with baby photos.

exEn: Everyone is wearing white student caps in the schoolyard.
note: The white sailor-style cap worn when you graduate from gymnasiet. Often just called mössan.

exEn: We ordered a sandwich cake for the graduation party.
note: A savory 'cake' of bread layered with shrimp, egg and mayonnaise, typical at birthdays and graduations.

ex: Vi firar {midsommar} hos vänner på landet.
exEn: We're celebrating Midsummer with friends in the countryside.
note: Often pronounced 'missommar'. The big party is on midsommarafton, a Friday in late June.

ex: På {midsommarafton} äter vi sill och jordgubbar.
exEn: On Midsummer Eve we eat herring and strawberries.
note: Always a Friday between 19 and 25 June, and in practice a day off for almost everyone.

exEn: Everyone dances around the maypole.
note: Also called majstång. In the classic dance, Små grodorna, everyone hops around like frogs.

exEn: Would you like some more herring?
note: Pickled herring (inlagd sill) with new potatoes is served at every big holiday.

ex: Ska vi ta en {snaps} till sillen?
exEn: Shall we have a schnapps with the herring?
note: A small shot, often of spiced aquavit. Also called nubbe. People sing a snapsvisa before drinking it.

ex: Innan vi skålar sjunger vi en {snapsvisa}.
exEn: Before we drink a toast, we sing a drinking song.
note: The most famous one is Helan går, sung before the first snaps.

exEn: We're having a crayfish party on Saturday.
note: An August party with crayfish, funny paper hats, snaps and songs. sk before i sounds like sj.

exEn: How many crayfish have you eaten?
note: Swedish crayfish are boiled with lots of dill and eaten cold.

exEn: Have you ever tasted fermented herring?
note: Baltic herring fermented in a can, famous for its smell. Open the can outdoors!

ex: Vi har en liten röd {stuga} vid sjön.
exEn: We have a little red cottage by the lake.
note: The classic stuga is painted falu red with white corners.

exEn: We're at the summer cottage all of July.
note: Many Swedish families have one, often in the countryside or the archipelago (skärgården).

ex: Hon köpte en röd {dalahäst} som souvenir.
exEn: She bought a red Dala horse as a souvenir.
note: A hand-painted wooden horse from Dalarna and a symbol of Sweden.

exEn: Where did you put my things?
note: The plural saker often means 'stuff'. Also 'matter': Det är en annan sak (That's another matter).

exEn: Wait, I forgot one thing!
note: Very common in speech; sak is more neutral. Grejen är att … = The thing is …

exEn: What a great idea!
note: Stressed on the é. Det är ingen idé = There's no point.

exEn: Thanks, that was a nice thought.
note: The final -e drops before the endings: tanken, tankar.

ex: Min {dröm} är att bo vid havet.
exEn: My dream is to live by the sea.
note: The m doubles before an ending: drömmen, drömmar.

exEn: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
note: Careful: ett plan is a plane (flygplan) or a floor/level in a building (plan 3).

ex: Finns det någon {anledning} att oroa sig?
exEn: Is there any reason to worry?
note: av den anledningen = for that reason

exEn: The police don't know the cause of the fire.
note: orsaken till något = the cause of something. Ingen orsak! = Don't mention it!

exEn: We have a problem with the car.
note: An ett-word with no plural ending: ett problem, två problem.

exEn: We have to find a solution.
In that case, I'll stay home.
note: i så fall = in that case; i alla fall = anyway, at least. It can also mean 'a fall'.

ex: Det är en svår {situation} för alla.
exEn: It's a difficult situation for everyone.
note: -tion is pronounced 'shoon' and carries the stress.

ex: Det här är en stor {möjlighet} för mig.
exEn: This is a big opportunity for me.
Give me one more chance!
note: A French loan: ch is the sj-sound, and the n usually sounds like ng.

exEn: I'm busy at the moment.
note: för tillfället = at the moment; vid tillfälle = when you get a chance.

ex: Det finns en {risk} att vi missar tåget.
exEn: There's a risk that we'll miss the train.
We were lucky with the weather.
note: ha tur = to be lucky; otur = bad luck. Det är din tur = It's your turn.

exEn: What's the difference between them?
note: sk before i is the sj-sound. Det gör ingen skillnad = It makes no difference.

ex: Det finns många {likheter} mellan svenska och norska.
exEn: There are many similarities between Swedish and Norwegian.
note: likheter och skillnader = similarities and differences

exEn: Can you give an example?
note: till exempel (t.ex.) = for example. The last e drops: exemplet, exemplen.

ex: Den första {delen} av filmen var bäst.
exEn: The first part of the movie was the best.
note: en del also means 'some': en del människor (some people).

exEn: What type of music do you like?
note: In casual speech typ also means 'like, sort of': Det tar typ en timme.

exEn: This kind is cheaper.
note: 'A kind of' is en sorts or ett slags: ett slags bröd.

ex: Det finns inget bättre {sätt} att lära sig.
exEn: There's no better way to learn.
note: på det sättet = that way; på något sätt = somehow. A way you walk or drive is en väg.

exEn: We're still waiting for the result.
What's the purpose of the meeting?
note: i syfte att = with the aim of (formal)

exEn: In the beginning it was hard.
note: Same form with and without 'the': i början av maj (at the beginning of May), en bra början (a good start).

exEn: Put the table in the middle of the room.
note: Mostly used as mitten: i mitten av juni (in the middle of June). Not to be confused with mitt (my).

exEn: The movie had a happy ending.
note: i slutet av maj = at the end of May. Also an adjective: Mjölken är slut (We're out of milk).

exEn: What do you want to do in the future?
That's a thing of the past.
note: Always with det. 'He has a past' is Han har ett förflutet.

ex: Det blir en stor {förändring} för barnen.
exEn: It will be a big change for the kids.
note: A small edit or correction is en ändring: en ändring i schemat (a change to the schedule).

exEn: It was a difficult decision.
note: fatta ett beslut = to make a decision

exEn: That was a good try!
note: The verb is försöka (to try).

exEn: You have to follow the rules.
note: The e of -el drops before an ending: regeln, regler. som regel = as a rule, usually.

exEn: Is everything all right?
note: i ordning = in order, OK: Det är i ordning (That's fine). An order in a shop or restaurant is en beställning.

exEn: It's your responsibility.
note: No plural. ta ansvar för = to take responsibility for; ansvarig = responsible.

exEn: He has a lot of power in the company.
note: Power over people. Physical strength is styrka; electric power is el or ström.

exEn: What are your strengths?
note: A classic job interview question, often followed by: Och dina svagheter?

exEn: Chocolate is my biggest weakness.

ex: Det finns ett stort {behov} av lärare.
exEn: There's a great need for teachers.
note: vid behov = when needed. The verb is behöva (to need).

exEn: She has a good knowledge of Swedish.
note: Often plural for knowledge of a subject: kunskaper i engelska.

ex: Jag har ett dåligt {minne} för namn.
exEn: I have a bad memory for names.
note: Both the ability (ett bra minne) and something remembered (fina minnen).

exEn: Tell the truth!
note: säga sanningen and tala sanning (no article) both mean 'to tell the truth'.

exEn: That's a lie!
note: gn sounds like ngn: 'löngn'. The verb is ljuga (to lie).

exEn: In reality, it's harder.
note: i verkligheten = in reality, in real life

exEn: Smoking is a bad habit.
note: av gammal vana = out of habit; van vid = used to

exEn: Let's keep in touch!
note: ta kontakt med = to get in touch with. Also an electric plug or socket.

ex: Jag har en bra {relation} till min chef.
exEn: I have a good relationship with my boss.
note: Note the preposition: en relation till någon.

ex: De har haft ett {förhållande} i två år.
exEn: They've been in a relationship for two years.
note: i förhållande till = in relation to; the plural förhållanden often means 'conditions'.

exEn: The word has two meanings.
note: Det har ingen betydelse = It doesn't matter. The verb is betyda (to mean).

exEn: The house has increased in value.
The food is of high quality.
note: Also spelled kvalité, pronounced without the final t.

ex: Vilken {nivå} är du på i svenska?
exEn: What level are you at in Swedish?
He drinks huge amounts of coffee.
note: For things you count, use antal: ett stort antal bilar (a large number of cars).

exEn: The number of tourists increases every year.
note: How many there are. A phone number is ett nummer; a digit is en siffra.

ex: En stor {fördel} är att det är nära.
exEn: A big advantage is that it's close by.
The downside is that it's expensive.
note: fördelar och nackdelar = pros and cons

ex: Mjölken smakar {konstigt}, den har nog gått ut.
exEn: The milk tastes funny; it's probably past its date.
note: Det är inte så konstigt = It's not surprising.

ex: Andersson är ett {vanligt} efternamn i Sverige.
exEn: Andersson is a common surname in Sweden.
note: som vanligt = as usual; vanligtvis = usually.

exEn: She has a very unusual name.

ex: Är det {normalt} att vara så här trött?
exEn: Is it normal to be this tired?
note: normalt = normally: Normalt jobbar jag hemifrån.

ex: Idag är en {speciell} dag för oss.
exEn: Today is a special day for us.
note: About a person it can mean odd: Han är lite speciell. Speciellt = especially.

exEn: Is there any particular reason?
note: Said 'sä-shild', with no k sound. särskilt = especially: särskilt på vintern.

exEn: Typical! The bus just left.
note: typisk för = typical of: Det är typiskt för honom.

ex: Jag och min bror är väldigt {olika}.
exEn: My brother and I are very different.
note: Never changes form. olika = different from each other, various; annorlunda = different from usual.

ex: Du ser {annorlunda} ut! Har du klippt dig?
exEn: You look different! Did you get a haircut?
note: Never changes form. annorlunda än = different from.

exEn: It's a bit complicated to explain.
note: Forms like a past participle: komplicerat, komplicerade.

exEn: The answer was clear: no.
note: Kan du prata tydligare? = Can you speak more clearly? tydligen = apparently.

exEn: What's the exact address?
note: Exakt! on its own = Exactly! Also an adverb: exakt klockan tre.

exEn: Is that your real hair color?
note: Riktigt is also an adverb: riktigt bra = really good; inte riktigt = not quite.

exEn: The film is based on a true story.
note: verkligen = really: Jag gillar det verkligen.

exEn: Is the bag genuine or fake?
note: Never changes form: ett äkta smycke, äkta läder.

exEn: He used a false name.
note: Also 'out of tune': sjunga falskt. About a person it means two-faced.

exEn: Perfect! See you at seven, then.
note: Stress on the second syllable: per-FEKT.

exEn: The view from here is fantastic.
Thanks for a wonderful evening!
What a lovely day!
note: Härligt! on its own = Great! / Lovely!

exEn: The match was exciting right to the end.
note: Never changes form: en spännande film, ett spännande jobb.

exEn: How interesting! Tell me more.
note: The neuter is the same, because the word already ends in -t: ett intressant jobb.

exEn: It was an incredible trip.
note: Otroligt is a very common intensifier: otroligt bra = incredibly good.

exEn: What terrible weather!
note: Also an intensifier in speech: hemskt mycket = an awful lot.

exEn: How nice to be home again!
note: sk before ö is the sj-sound. Skönt! on its own = What a relief! / Nice!

exEn: These shoes are so comfortable.
note: bekväm av sig = a bit lazy, fond of comfort.

ex: Det kändes lite {obekvämt} att säga nej.
exEn: It felt a bit awkward to say no.

ex: Det är väldigt {praktiskt} att bo nära jobbet.
exEn: It's really convenient to live close to work.
note: praktiskt taget = practically, almost.

ex: Det här är en {användbar} fras att kunna.
exEn: This is a useful phrase to know.
note: From använda (to use) + -bar (-able).

exEn: Is that really necessary?
note: inte nödvändigtvis = not necessarily.

ex: Det är {onödigt} att ta bilen, vi kan gå.
exEn: There's no need to take the car; we can walk.

ex: Har vi {tillräckligt} med mat för alla?
exEn: Do we have enough food for everyone?
note: tillräckligt bra = good enough.

exEn: Let me know when you're done!
note: Also 'clear': en klar himmel. Ja, klart! = Sure! Of course!

exEn: The house will be finished in May.
note: Often the same as klar: Jag är klar/färdig = I'm done.

exEn: Is everyone ready? Then let's go!
note: Never changes form: Allt är redo. Vi är redo.

ex: Är du {beredd} att flytta för jobbet?
exEn: Are you willing to move for the job?
note: beredd att = prepared to, willing to. Neuter: berett.

exEn: Excuse me, is this seat free?
note: Jag är ledig imorgon = I'm off (work) tomorrow. 'Free of charge' is gratis.

exEn: I'm a bit busy right now.
note: Det är upptaget = It's occupied (toilet) or busy (phone line). Plural: upptagna.

exEn: The app is available in English too.
note: Also 'accessible', for example for wheelchair users.

exEn: Sweden is a free country.
note: Neuter: fritt. 'Free of charge' is gratis; 'free (not busy)' is ledig.

exEn: Admission to the museum is free.
note: Never changes form: gratis kaffe, gratis parkering.

exEn: I want my own room.
note: Irregular: mitt eget rum, mina egna barn.

exEn: May I ask a personal question?
note: personligen = personally.

exEn: This is a private road.
note: The neuter is the same: ett privat samtal.

exEn: There are public toilets by the square.
note: den offentliga sektorn = the public sector.

exEn: We have a mutual friend.
note: Double m before an ending: gemensamma. en gemensam tvättstuga = a shared laundry room.

exEn: It was in the local paper.
note: Also a noun: en lokal = premises, a venue.

exEn: Is the information on the website up to date?
note: False friend: 'actual' is verklig. Aktuell means current or up to date.

exEn: The kitchen is new and modern.
note: Stress on the second syllable: mo-DÄRN.

exEn: My dad is a bit old-fashioned.
note: Never changes form: ett gammaldags kök.

exEn: The restaurant is popular, so book a table.

ex: Sverige är {känt} för IKEA och ABBA.
exEn: Sweden is famous for IKEA and ABBA.
note: Neuter: känt. A celebrity is en kändis.

ex: Jag fick ett samtal från ett {okänt} nummer.
exEn: I got a call from an unknown number.
She became famous overnight.
note: Känd is more common in everyday speech.

exEn: Of course you can come along!
note: Det är självklart = That goes without saying. Självklart! on its own = Of course!

exEn: I don't know if I'll have time.
note: veta = to know a fact; to know a person is känna. Casually just: Vet inte.

ex: – Vem vann matchen? – {Ingen aning}, jag såg den inte.
exEn: – Who won the game? – No idea, I didn't see it.
note: aning = hunch, notion. Full sentence: Jag har ingen aning.

ex: – Kan du hämta mig vid stationen? – {Inga problem}!
exEn: – Can you pick me up at the station? – No problem!
note: problem is the same in the plural: ett problem, två problem.

ex: – Förlåt att jag är sen! – {Ingen fara}, vi har inte börjat än.
exEn: – Sorry I'm late! – No worries, we haven't started yet.
note: Literally 'no danger'. A kind reply to an apology.

ex: – Ska jag hjälpa dig? – Nej tack, {det är lugnt}.
exEn: – Shall I help you? – No thanks, it's fine.
note: Literally 'it's calm'. A relaxed reply to thanks, apologies and offers.

ex: – Jag glömde din bok. – {Det gör inget}, ta med den imorgon.
exEn: – I forgot your book. – It doesn't matter, bring it tomorrow.
note: Also: Det gör inget om du är sen (It's OK if you're late).

ex: {Det spelar ingen roll} vad andra tycker.
exEn: It doesn't matter what other people think.
note: Literally 'it plays no role'. Spelar det någon roll? = Does it matter?

en: it's not the end of the world
alt: not the end of the world
ex: Vi förlorade, men {det är inte hela världen}.
exEn: We lost, but it's not the end of the world.
note: Literally 'it's not the whole world'.

ex: – Jag mår mycket bättre nu. – {Vad bra}!
exEn: – I feel much better now. – That's good!
note: vad + adjective in the ett-form = how …!: Vad skönt! (What a relief!), Vad gulligt! (How cute!)

ex: – Vi ska gifta oss! – Åh, {vad roligt}!
exEn: – We're getting married! – Oh, how lovely!
note: Said when you hear good news. Vad kul! means the same and is just as common. The g in roligt is silent.

ex: – Jag kan inte komma på festen. – {Vad synd}!
exEn: – I can't come to the party. – What a shame!
note: synd also means 'sin'. Det är synd om honom = I feel sorry for him.

exEn: – I'll sort out the tickets. – Great, thanks!
note: Literally 'the top'. Also: Det var toppen! (It was great!)

exEn: Oops, sorry! I didn't mean to.
note: Shows surprise or a small mistake. Oj då! = Oops! / Oh dear!

exEn: Ugh, it's so cold today!
note: Shows dislike or disgust: Usch, vad äckligt! (Yuck, how gross!)

ex: – Jag ska flytta till Norge. – {Jaså}? När då?
exEn: – I'm moving to Norway. – Really? When?
note: Shows surprise or interest in news. Pronounced 'jasså'.

exEn: What? You've sold the car?
note: Casual. More polite: Förlåt? or Vad sa du? Also a tag at the end: Snyggt, va? (Nice, huh?)

ex: – Filmen var för lång. – Ja, {jag håller med}.
exEn: – The movie was too long. – Yes, I agree.
note: From hålla med (to agree), with stress on med. Jag håller med dig = I agree with you.

ex: – Bor du i Uppsala? – Ja, {det stämmer}.
exEn: – Do you live in Uppsala? – Yes, that's right.
note: stämma = to be correct, to add up. Stämmer det? = Is that right?

exEn: – So we'll meet at six? – Exactly!
note: As an adverb it also means 'just': precis som jag (just like me), Jag kom precis hem (I just got home).

exEn: – Can I borrow your bike? – Absolutely!
note: Absolut inte! = Absolutely not! / No way!

exEn: – May I sit here? – Sure!
note: visst also asks for agreement: Visst är det fint här? (Isn't it lovely here?)

exEn: She won, of course, as usual.
note: Also written såklart. Självklart means the same.

ex: – Ska vi ses vid sju? – {Det låter bra}!
exEn: – Shall we meet at seven? – Sounds good!
note: låta = to sound. Det låter kul! = Sounds fun!

exEn: It's cold today, isn't it?
note: Like English isn't it? or don't you?, but it never changes form.

ex: – Kommer du imorgon? – {Det beror på} vädret.
exEn: – Are you coming tomorrow? – It depends on the weather.
note: bero på = to depend on; also 'to be due to': Förseningen beror på snön (The delay is due to the snow).

exEn: – Have you eaten? – No, not yet.
note: In a full sentence än usually comes last: Jag har inte ätit än. Also: inte ännu.

ex: Vi kan äta något enkelt, {typ} pasta.
exEn: We can eat something simple, like pasta.
note: Very common in casual speech (Det tar typ en timme = It takes about an hour). Avoid it in formal writing.

exEn: It was, like, a bit weird.
note: A filler word in casual speech. In formal Swedish it means 'like; as': liksom förra året (as last year).

ex: {Hur som helst}, nu måste jag gå.
exEn: Anyway, I have to go now.
note: Also 'any old way': Man kan inte parkera hur som helst (You can't park any old way).

ex: Det regnade, men vi hade kul {i alla fall}.
exEn: It rained, but we had fun anyway.
note: Also 'at least': Det var i alla fall gratis (At least it was free). In texts often iaf.

exEn: Happy birthday!
note: Short for gratulerar. Used for birthdays, new jobs, passed exams and so on.

exEn: Good luck with the test tomorrow!
note: lycka means both luck and happiness.

ex: Jag hörde att du är sjuk. {Krya på dig}!
exEn: I heard you're sick. Get well soon!
note: From krya på sig (to get better). To several people: Krya på er!

ex: {Bra jobbat}, allihop! Nu är vi klara.
exEn: Well done, everyone! We're finished now.
note: jobbat is the supine of jobba (to work). Also common: Snyggt jobbat!

ex: Här är ditt kvitto. {Ha en bra dag}!
exEn: Here's your receipt. Have a nice day!
note: Typical reply: Tack, detsamma! (Thanks, you too!)

ex: Ska ni till Paris? {Ha det så kul}!
exEn: Are you going to Paris? Have fun!
note: Also: Ha så kul! or Ha det så roligt!

exEn: Good night, darling. Sleep well!
note: sov is the imperative of sova (to sleep); gott here means 'well'.

exEn: – Have a nice weekend! – Thanks, you too!
note: The usual reply to good wishes like Trevlig helg! or Ha en bra dag!, often as Tack, detsamma!

ex: Barn, glöm inte att säga {tack för maten}!
exEn: Kids, don't forget to say thank you for the meal!
note: Said to the host, or whoever cooked, when you get up from the table.

ex: {Tack för senast}! Det var en jättetrevlig kväll.
exEn: Thanks for the other night! It was a really lovely evening.
note: Said the next time you see someone you spent time with, for example after a dinner at their place. A key part of Swedish politeness.

exEn: It's been ages since we last saw each other!
note: sedan is usually said (and often written) sen here. Literally 'it was long ago'.

exEn: How did the job interview go?
note: gick is the past tense of gå. Answer: Det gick bra! (It went well!)

exEn: Hi! What are you doing this weekend?
note: For someone's job, Swedes usually ask: Vad jobbar du med?

en: how do you say … in Swedish?
alt: how do you say in Swedish
how do you say it in Swedish
how do you say that in Swedish
exEn: How do you say "spoon" in Swedish?
note: man = one, people in general. Also common: Vad heter … på svenska?

exEn: Excuse me, what does this word mean?
note: betyda = to mean. Vad menar du? = What do you mean (by that)?

ex: Förlåt, jag hörde inte. {Kan du upprepa det}?
exEn: Sorry, I didn't hear. Can you repeat that?
note: More casual: Kan du säga det igen?

ex: {Ta det lugnt}, vi har gott om tid.
exEn: Take it easy, we have plenty of time.
note: Also a casual goodbye: Hej då, ta det lugnt!

ex: {Skynda dig}, bussen går om två minuter!
exEn: Hurry up, the bus leaves in two minutes!
note: sk before y is the sj-sound. To several people: Skynda er!

exEn: Watch out, the floor is slippery!
note: Akta dig för hunden! = Watch out for the dog! To several people: Akta er!

ex: {Vänta lite}, jag ska bara hämta jackan.
exEn: Wait a moment, I'm just going to get my jacket.
note: More formal: Ett ögonblick! (One moment!)

ex: Hon har alltid varit intresserad av {konst}.
exEn: She has always been interested in art.
note: Det är ingen konst! = It's easy, there's nothing to it. A painter or sculptor is en konstnär.

ex: Den här {målningen} är över hundra år gammal.
exEn: This painting is over a hundred years old.
note: A painting on the wall is often just called en tavla.

ex: Det här är museets mest kända {konstverk}.
exEn: This is the museum's most famous work of art.
note: Same form in the plural: ett konstverk, två konstverk.

ex: Museet har en ny {utställning} om vikingatiden.
exEn: The museum has a new exhibition about the Viking Age.

ex: Jag vill ha ett mer {kreativt} jobb.
exEn: I want a more creative job.
note: Stress on the last syllable: kre-a-TIV.

exEn: What kind of music do you like?
note: Stress on the second syllable: mu-SIK.

exEn: I love this song!
note: The everyday word for a song or track. Also the imperative of låta: Låt mig! = Let me!

exEn: We sang a song for Grandma.
note: Also singing: Hon studerar sång. For a pop song or track, låt is more common.

exEn: He's a singer in a rock band.
note: A female singer is often called en sångerska.

exEn: Which artist do you listen to the most?
note: False friend: en artist is a performer, like a singer. A painter is en konstnär.

exEn: She works as a musician in Stockholm.
note: Same form in the plural: en musiker, två musiker.

ex: Vi startade ett {band} när vi gick i skolan.
exEn: We started a band when we were in school.
note: Same form in the plural: ett band, två band.

ex: Min mamma sjunger i {kör} varje torsdag.
exEn: My mom sings in a choir every Thursday.
note: Hard k here, unlike kör (drive!) from köra, which starts with the tj-sound.

ex: Vi ska gå på {konsert} i helgen.
exEn: We're going to a concert this weekend.
note: The t is silent in konsert ('kon-SÄR'), but you hear it in konserten.

exEn: Do you play an instrument?

ex: Jag har spelat {gitarr} i fem år.
exEn: I've been playing the guitar for five years.
note: The g is soft: 'yi-TARR'. No article: spela gitarr = play the guitar.

ex: Min son vill lära sig spela {piano}.
exEn: My son wants to learn to play the piano.
The neighbor's son plays the drums all day long.
note: To play the drums = spela trummor (plural, no article).

ex: Min dotter spelar {fiol} i skolans orkester.
exEn: My daughter plays the violin in the school orchestra.
note: En violin also exists, but fiol is the everyday word.

ex: Bandet ska {spela in} ett nytt album i vår.
exEn: The band is going to record a new album this spring.
note: Particle verb: the stress is on in. A recording is en inspelning.

exEn: Can you turn the sound down a bit?
note: lj is pronounced j: 'yood'.

ex: Ska vi se en {film} i kväll?
exEn: Shall we watch a movie tonight?
note: Watch a movie = se (or titta på) en film.

ex: Jag har börjat titta på en ny {serie}.
exEn: I've started watching a new series.
note: Also a comic strip. A comic book is en serietidning.

ex: Vi såg tre {avsnitt} på en kväll.
exEn: We watched three episodes in one evening.
note: Same form in the plural: ett avsnitt, tre avsnitt.

exEn: She dreams of becoming an actor.
note: Used for both men and women. Skådespelerska (actress) also exists.

exEn: The movie's director is from Gothenburg.
note: The g is pronounced with the sj-sound: 're-shi-SÖR'.

ex: Han fick en liten {roll} i filmen.
exEn: He got a small part in the movie.
note: Det spelar ingen roll = It doesn't matter.

ex: Jag såg en {kändis} på tåget i morse.
exEn: I saw a celebrity on the train this morning.
note: From känd (famous). The k is soft: tj-sound.

exEn: We saw a play by Strindberg.
The show starts at seven.

ex: Bandet gick upp på {scenen} klockan nio.
exEn: The band went on stage at nine o'clock.
note: sc is pronounced s. Also a scene in a movie or play.

ex: {Publiken} klappade i händerna och sjöng med.
exEn: The audience clapped and sang along.
note: False friend: publik means audience. 'The public' is allmänheten.

exEn: Give her a big round of applause!
note: Often in the plural: långa applåder. To applaud = applådera.

ex: Vad blir det på {tv} i kväll?
exEn: What's on TV tonight?
note: Pronounced 'teve'. Watch TV = titta på tv. The plural is usually tv-apparater (TV sets).

exEn: I listen to the radio in the car.
note: No article: lyssna på radio. The plural is usually radioapparater (radio sets).

exEn: Which show are you watching?
note: Double m in the definite forms: programmet, programmen.

ex: Det är så mycket {reklam} på tv nu.
exEn: There are so many ads on TV these days.
note: Uncountable. A single TV ad is en reklamfilm; an ad in print is en annons.

ex: Jag lyssnar på {poddar} när jag tränar.
exEn: I listen to podcasts when I work out.
note: Also called en podcast.

exEn: The movie got good reviews.
note: To review = recensera.

ex: Det blir mat, musik och {underhållning} hela kvällen.
exEn: There will be food, music and entertainment all evening.
note: From underhålla = to entertain.

exEn: She's writing her first novel.
note: False friend: en roman is a novel, not a romance.

ex: Astrid Lindgren är en känd svensk {författare}.
exEn: Astrid Lindgren is a famous Swedish author.
The book is based on a true story.
note: From berätta = to tell.

ex: Han skrev en {dikt} till sin fru.
exEn: He wrote a poem for his wife.
note: Poetry is poesi or lyrik.
